title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄序
成化庚子秋式當試士
上命翰林院侍講學士臣楊守陳
右春坊右諭德臣陸簡主
京師順天府試事順天與畿
內七郡合六舘諸司士就試
者凡三千六百有竒論其秀
===
僅得一百三十五人遵
定額也惟九州之域風氣習
尚皆異古之帝王一道德同
風俗亦必乆而後浹焉
大明輿圖曠古所未有而
兩京對峙于南北蓋自
太祖高皇帝都應天府尋號南京
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄序

成化庚子秋，式當試士，上命翰林院侍講學士臣楊守陳、右春坊右諭德臣陸簡主京師順天府試事。順天與畿內七郡，合六舘諸司士，就試者凡三千六百有竒。論其秀，僅得一百三十五人，遵定額也。

惟九州之域，風氣習尚皆異。古之帝王一道德、同風俗，亦必乆而後浹焉。大明輿圖，曠古所未有，而兩京對峙于南北。蓋自太祖高皇帝都應天府，尋號南京，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the gengzi year of Chenghua [1480], when the prescribed time came to examine scholars, His Majesty commanded your servant Yang Shouchen, Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, and your servant Lu Jian, Right Mentor of the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, to preside over the examination at Shuntian Prefecture, the imperial capital. Candidates from Shuntian and the seven prefectures within the metropolitan region, together with scholars from the Six Colleges and the various government offices, numbered more than 3,600 in all. Upon assessing their outstanding men, only 135 were selected, in accordance with the established quota.

Throughout the Nine Provinces, local dispositions, customs, and preferences all differ. Even the sage emperors and kings of antiquity, in unifying moral principles and making customs uniform, necessarily required a long time before their influence permeated everywhere. The territory of the Great Ming is unprecedented in all antiquity, and its two capitals stand facing one another in the south and north. This began when Emperor Taizu Gao established his capital at Yingtian Prefecture, which was subsequently designated Nanjing…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
太宗文皇帝即順天府爲北京至
于今都焉臣守陳往歲嘗被
旨論秀于應天今復論順天之
秀於是兩京之士皆得而悉
之其秀之蕃衍碩大盖非四
方萬國所能踰也然應天在
江左由司馬晉至後唐凡八
===
代屢嘗建都而隣郡亦嘗爲
輔至
國初仍作京畿政敎之洊重文
獻之稠疊宜其秀之蕃且碩
矣順天在冀方與今畿內數
郡自石晉沒于遼以迄于金
元歷四百三十有餘歲遭我
punctuated: 太宗文皇帝即順天府爲北京，至于今都焉。臣守陳往歲嘗被旨論秀于應天，今復論順天之秀，於是兩京之士皆得而悉之。其秀之蕃衍碩大，盖非四方萬國所能踰也。然應天在江左，由司馬晉至後唐，凡八代，屢嘗建都，而隣郡亦嘗爲輔。至國初，仍作京畿，政敎之洊重，文獻之稠疊，宜其秀之蕃且碩矣。順天在冀方，與今畿內數郡，自石晉沒于遼，以迄于金、元，歷四百三十有餘歲，遭我
translation_en:
Emperor Wen, Taizong, made Shuntian Prefecture the northern capital, Beijing, and it has remained the capital to this day. In past years, your servant Shouchen received an imperial command to assess the outstanding talent at Yingtian; now I have again assessed the outstanding talent at Shuntian. Thus I have had the opportunity to become thoroughly acquainted with the scholars of both capitals. The abundance and stature of their outstanding talent can scarcely be surpassed anywhere in the realm or among the myriad countries.

Yingtian, however, lies in Jiangzuo, south of the Yangzi. From the Jin of the Sima house to the Later Tang [?], through eight dynasties in all, it repeatedly served as the capital, while neighboring prefectures served as its supporting region. At the founding of our dynasty, it again became the capital region. With successive layers of government and moral instruction, and a rich accumulation of writings and worthy men, it is fitting that its outstanding talent should be both abundant and distinguished.

Shuntian lies in the region of Ji. Together with several prefectures now within the capital region, it fell to the Liao during the Jin of the Shi house and remained under the Jin and Yuan, a period of more than four hundred and thirty years, before coming under our …

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖朝乃始復歸于華夏新化雖洽
舊俗或遺今其秀乃與應天
諸郡並蕃而齊碩者何居守
陳聞之燕有谷寒不生黍鄒
衍吹律以溫其氣而黍生焉
况有大於律者其所生豈特
黍而已哉自我
===
神祖掃胡俗以復華風
列聖丕承德洋仁普逮今百稔餘
矣正所謂聖人久於其道而
天下化成故雖月窟日域氷
天炎海之外亦皆漸被變遷
而况順天諸郡乃
日月之所近臨也風霆之所先
punctuated: 聖朝乃始復歸于華夏。新化雖洽，舊俗或遺。今其秀乃與應天諸郡並蕃而齊碩者，何居？守陳聞之：燕有谷，寒不生黍，鄒衍吹律以溫其氣，而黍生焉。况有大於律者，其所生豈特黍而已哉？自我神祖掃胡俗以復華風，列聖丕承，德洋仁普，逮今百稔餘矣。正所謂聖人久於其道，而天下化成。故雖月窟日域、氷天炎海之外，亦皆漸被變遷，而况順天諸郡，乃日月之所近臨也，風霆之所先
translation_en:
…under our sagely dynasty, it at last returned to the Chinese realm. Although the new civilizing influence has spread throughout, some old customs may remain. How is it, then, that its outstanding men now equal those of the prefectures of Yingtian in both abundance and stature? I, Shouchen, have heard this: in Yan there was a valley so cold that millet would not grow. Zou Yan blew a pitch pipe to warm its air, and millet grew there. How much more must this be true of something greater than a pitch pipe! Could what it brings forth be merely millet?

Since our Divine Progenitor swept away barbarian customs and restored Chinese ways, successive sage emperors have magnificently carried on his work. Their virtue is vast and their benevolence universal; more than a hundred years have now passed. This is precisely what is meant by the saying, “The sage perseveres in his Way, and the transformation of all under Heaven is accomplished.” Thus even lands beyond the moon’s cavern and the sun’s domain, beyond icy skies and burning seas, have all gradually received this influence and undergone transformation. How much more, then, the prefectures of Shuntian, upon which the sun and moon shine from close at hand, and where wind and thunder first…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
鼓也雨露之所偏渥也其秀
蕃碩不亦宜哉然秀於昔者
率能振芳英敷茂實以無負
乎
大造矣今之秀將與秀於昔者
爭芳而四方萬國之秀復與
秀於京者競茂舉
===
明世於三代之隆固
丕基於億年之久不在茲乎試
畢錄成守陳當序故道
兩京之秀之蕃碩以見
神聖功化若此其隆俾天下皆興
後世皆慕焉若夫勗厲士子
之詞已屢發於前人而同考
punctuated:
鼓也，雨露之所偏渥也，其秀蕃碩，不亦宜哉？然秀於昔者，率能振芳英，敷茂實，以無負乎大造矣。今之秀，將與秀於昔者爭芳，而四方萬國之秀，復與秀於京者競茂。舉明世於三代之隆，固丕基於億年之久，不在茲乎？
試畢，錄成，守陳當序，故道兩京之秀之蕃碩，以見神聖功化若此其隆，俾天下皆興，後世皆慕焉。若夫勗厲士子之詞，已屢發於前人，而同考
translation_en:
…stirred by wind and thunder, and especially richly nourished by rain and dew. Is it not fitting that its outstanding talents should be so abundant and flourishing? The outstanding men of former times were generally able to display fragrant blossoms and bear abundant fruit, thus proving worthy of the great bounty bestowed upon them. Today’s outstanding men will vie in fragrance with those of the past, while outstanding men from every quarter and every realm will in turn compete in luxuriance with those of the capital. Does not raising this enlightened age to the flourishing heights of the Three Dynasties, and securing its great foundation for a hundred million years, depend upon this?
The examination concluded and the record completed, it falls to me, Yang Shouchen, to write the preface. I have therefore described the abundance and flourishing of outstanding talent in the two capitals, to show how magnificent are the achievements and transforming influence of our sagely sovereigns, so that all under Heaven may be inspired and later generations may look upon them with admiration. As for words exhorting and encouraging the candidates, these have already been expressed repeatedly by my predecessors; and as for the Associate Examiners…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
先事後得非崇德與
辟如四時之錯行如日月之代明
心之所同然者何也謂理也義也聖人先
得我心之所同然耳故理義之悅我
心猶芻豢之悅我口
易
大君之宜行中之謂也
===
剛柔分動而明雷電合而章柔得中而上
行
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉夫
坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉
二與四同功而異位其善不同
書
天秩有禮自我五禮有庸哉
若升高必自下若陟遐必自邇
若稽田既勤敷菑惟其陳修爲厥疆畎
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
先事後得，非崇德與？
辟如四時之錯行，如日月之代明。
心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。故理義之悅我心，猶芻豢之悅我口。

易
大君之宜，行中之謂也。
剛柔分，動而明，雷電合而章，柔得中而上行。
夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。
二與四同功而異位，其善不同。

書
天秩有禮，自我五禮有庸哉！
若升高，必自下；若陟遐，必自邇。
若稽田，既勤敷菑，惟其陳修，爲厥疆畎。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
To put the work first and its rewards afterward—is this not to exalt virtue?
Like the four seasons proceeding in turn, like the sun and moon shining alternately.
What is it that our hearts alike approve? It is principle and righteousness. The sage has merely apprehended before us what our hearts alike approve. Thus principle and righteousness delight my heart just as the meat of grass-fed and grain-fed animals delights my palate.

Book of Changes
What is fitting for a great ruler means acting in accordance with the mean.
The firm and yielding are distinguished; movement is joined with clarity. Thunder and lightning unite and become manifest. The yielding attains the central position and moves upward.
Qian, in stillness, is concentrated; in movement, it is direct. Thus it brings forth greatness. Kun, in stillness, is closed; in movement, it opens. Thus it brings forth breadth.
The second and fourth lines have the same function but different positions; their goodness is not the same.

Book of Documents
Heaven has ordered the rites; it is for us to put the five rites into practice!
If you would ascend a height, you must begin below; if you would travel far, you must begin nearby.
Consider cultivating a field: having diligently opened up the uncultivated ground, attend to its established cultivation, making its boundaries and drainage channels.

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
士制百姓于刑之中以敎祗德穆穆在上
明明在下灼于四方罔不惟德之勤
故乃明于刑之中率乂于民棐彝
詩
方叔涖止其車三千師干之試
文王受命有此武功
令儀令色小心翼翼古訓是式威儀是力
天子是若明命使賦
假哉皇考綏予孝子宣哲維人文武維后
===
燕及皇天克昌厥後綏我眉壽介以
繁祉既右烈考亦右文母
春秋
公及齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
會王世子于首止〔僖公五年〕公會宰
周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
突歸于鄭〔桓公十一年〕齊小白入于齊〔莊
公九年〕
punctuated:
士制百姓于刑之中，以敎祗德。穆穆在上，明明在下，灼于四方，罔不惟德之勤。
故乃明于刑之中，率乂于民，棐彝。

詩
方叔涖止，其車三千，師干之試。
文王受命，有此武功。
令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力。天子是若，明命使賦。
假哉皇考！綏予孝子。宣哲維人，文武維后。燕及皇天，克昌厥後。綏我眉壽，介以繁祉。既右烈考，亦右文母。

春秋
公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯，會王世子于首止。〔僖公五年〕公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
突歸于鄭。〔桓公十一年〕齊小白入于齊。〔莊公九年〕
translation_en:
The judicial officers regulated the common people through the proper application of punishments, teaching them to revere virtue. The ruler above was solemn and reverent; his ministers below were discerning and enlightened. Their influence shone throughout the four quarters, and none failed to devote themselves diligently to virtue.
Thus they understood the proper application of punishments, guided and governed the people, and upheld the constant norms.

Book of Odes
Fang Shu arrived with his three thousand chariots, his hosts and shields put to the test.
King Wen received the Mandate and achieved these martial successes.
Admirable in bearing and countenance, he was cautious and reverent. He took ancient teachings as his model and diligently cultivated dignified deportment. The Son of Heaven approved him and expressly commanded him to promulgate his decrees.
Great indeed is my august deceased father! He brings peace to me, his filial son. Enlightened and wise were his men; accomplished in civil and military affairs was their lord. His peaceful influence reached august Heaven, and he made his descendants flourish. Grant me the peace of long life and aid me with abundant blessings. Having honored my illustrious deceased father, I also honor my accomplished mother.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the king’s heir apparent at Shouzhi. 〔Fifth year of Duke Xi.〕 The duke met the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the heir of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕
Tu returned to Zheng. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan.〕 Xiaobai of Qi entered Qi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
滅項僖公十七年取鄟成公六年取邿襄
公十三年取鄫昭公四年
晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽僖公三十三年
禮記
一有元良萬國以貞
故聖人參於天地並於鬼神以治政也處
其所存禮之序也玩其所樂民之治
也故天生時而地生財人其父生而
師教之四者君以正用之故君者立
===
於無過之地也
賓入大門而奏肆夏示易以敬也
察於此四者可以有志於本矣
第貳塲
論
帝王以人文化成天下
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢文帝令郡國無來獻詔元年
punctuated:
滅項，僖公十七年；取鄟，成公六年；取邿，襄公十三年；取鄫，昭公四年。
晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽，僖公三十三年。

禮記
一有元良，萬國以貞。
故聖人參於天地，並於鬼神，以治政也。處其所存，禮之序也；玩其所樂，民之治也。故天生時而地生財，人其父生而師教之，四者君以正用之。故君者立於無過之地也。
賓入大門而奏肆夏，示易以敬也。
察於此四者，可以有志於本矣。

第貳塲
論
帝王以人文化成天下。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢文帝令郡國無來獻詔，元年。
translation_en:
Xiang was destroyed. Seventeenth year of Duke Xi.
Zhuan was taken. Sixth year of Duke Cheng.
Shi was taken. Thirteenth year of Duke Xiang.
Zeng was taken. Fourth year of Duke Zhao.
The men of Jin and the Jiang Rong defeated Qin at Yao. Thirty-third year of Duke Xi.

Record of Rites
Once there is a supremely good heir, the myriad states are thereby set right.
Thus the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth and stands alongside the spirits in conducting government. His abiding in what he preserves establishes the proper ordering of ritual; his taking delight in what he enjoys brings order to the people. Heaven produces the seasons, and Earth produces resources; a person's father gives him life, and his teacher instructs him. The ruler makes proper use of these four. Thus the ruler stands in a position free from error.
When the guest enters the main gate, the Si Xia is played, expressing ease together with reverence.
By examining these four things, one can direct one's aspirations toward the root.

Second Session
Discourse
Emperors and kings transform and perfect all under Heaven through cultural refinement.
One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Wen of Han ordering the commanderies and kingdoms to send no offerings. First year of his reign.

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥貞觀十六年
擬謝
賜續資治通鑑綱目表
判語五道
舉用有過官吏
隱匿費用稅粮課物
術士妄言禍福
官司出入人罪
虛費功力採取不堪用
===
第叁場
策五道
問穆叔有言太上立德其次立功其次立
言說者謂黃帝堯舜為立德禹稷為立
功史佚周任臧文仲為立言未之盡也
夫德立固上矣然功也言也非德曷能
立耶朱子謂道德文章不可使為二然
則德與功言其可使為三乎黃帝神靈
徇齊堯欽明文思安安舜温恭允塞德
punctuated:
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥，貞觀十六年。
擬謝賜續資治通鑑綱目表。
判語五道：
舉用有過官吏。
隱匿費用稅粮課物。
術士妄言禍福。
官司出入人罪。
虛費功力採取不堪用。

第叁場
策五道
問：穆叔有言：「太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。」說者謂黃帝、堯、舜為立德，禹、稷為立功，史佚、周任、臧文仲為立言，未之盡也。夫德立固上矣，然功也、言也，非德曷能立耶？朱子謂：「道德文章不可使為二。」然則德與功、言，其可使為三乎？黃帝神靈徇齊，堯欽明文思安安，舜温恭允塞，德
translation_en:
Compose a proclamation in the name of the Tang court appointing Wei Zheng Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, dated to the sixteenth year of Zhenguan.
Compose a memorial expressing thanks for the bestowal of the Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Xu Zizhi tongjian gangmu).
Five legal judgments:
Recommending and appointing officials and clerks who have committed offenses.
Concealing or expending tax grain and goods collected as taxes.
Diviners making unfounded predictions of misfortune and good fortune.
Judicial authorities wrongly imposing or removing criminal liability.
Wasting labor in procuring materials unfit for use.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: Mushu said: “Highest is establishing virtue; next is establishing achievements; next is establishing words.” Commentators say that the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun exemplified establishing virtue; Yu and Ji, establishing achievements; and Shi Yi, Zhou Ren, and Zang Wenzhong, establishing words. This does not exhaust the matter. Establishing virtue is certainly highest; yet how could achievements or words be established without virtue? Master Zhu said: “The Way and virtue, and literary composition, must not be made into two separate things.” Can virtue, achievements, and words, then, be made into three separate things? The Yellow Emperor possessed divine intelligence and keen discernment; Yao was reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful, naturally at ease in these qualities; Shun was gentle, respectful, and truly sincere. Their virtue…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
固立矣而其功若畫埜分州若曆象定
時若封山濬川其言若書契若二典所
載皆不可謂不立也禹平水土稷播百
穀功固立矣而其德若克勤于邦若克
配彼天其言若虞書二謨亦皆不可謂
不立也若夫史周臧三子其言比之聖
人猶霄壤也其可獨謂其立言而以次
於數聖人耶是或有說矣自禹而降若
殷周漢唐宋諸君亦有德功言可與數
===
聖人並者歟逮我
皇明
一祖四宗皆以上聖之資當大造之任其德功
言俱與數聖人同矣可得究其詳歟夫
天地之德化育之功奎璧之章固萬國之所
共覩而齊聞者况在京畿之内者哉是
不可讓矣
問古之爲民者四曰士農工商外此無他
民也故四民安則天下治矣古之帝王
punctuated:
固立矣，而其功若畫埜分州，若曆象定時，若封山濬川；其言若書契，若二典所載，皆不可謂不立也。禹平水土，稷播百穀，功固立矣，而其德若克勤于邦，若克配彼天；其言若虞書二謨，亦皆不可謂不立也。若夫史、周、臧三子，其言比之聖人，猶霄壤也，其可獨謂其立言，而以次於數聖人耶？是或有說矣。自禹而降，若殷、周、漢、唐、宋諸君，亦有德、功、言可與數聖人並者歟？逮我皇明，一祖四宗皆以上聖之資，當大造之任，其德、功、言俱與數聖人同矣，可得究其詳歟？夫天地之德、化育之功、奎璧之章，固萬國之所共覩而齊聞者，况在京畿之内者哉！是不可讓矣。
問：古之爲民者四，曰士、農、工、商，外此無他民也。故四民安，則天下治矣。古之帝王
translation_en:
…their virtue was indeed established. Yet their achievements—demarcating the land and dividing it into provinces, observing and calculating the celestial movements to determine the seasons, marking out the mountains and dredging the rivers—and their words, whether in written records or as recorded in the Two Canons, cannot be said to have failed to endure either. Yu brought the waters and lands into order, and Ji sowed the various grains: their achievements were indeed established. Yet their virtue, exemplified by being “diligent in the affairs of the state” and “worthy to be matched with Heaven,” and their words, as in the two Counsels of the Book of Yu, likewise cannot be said to have failed to endure. As for the three men Shi Yi, Zhou Ren, and Zang Wenzhong, the distance between their words and those of the sages is like that between heaven and earth. How can one single them out as having established enduring words and thereby rank them next after those several sages? There may be an explanation for this. From Yu onward, among the rulers of the Yin, Zhou, Han, Tang, and Song, were there also any whose virtue, achievements, and words could stand alongside those of these sages?
Coming down to our august Ming, the one founding ancestor and four ancestral sovereigns all possessed the qualities of supreme sages and bore responsibility for the great work of creation. Their virtue, achievements, and words all equal those of these sages. Can you investigate the particulars? Their virtue, like that of Heaven and Earth, their achievements in transforming and nurturing, and their literary brilliance, like that of the Kui and Bi constellations, are surely seen and heard alike throughout the myriad lands. How much more must this be so for those within the metropolitan region! You must not yield to others in addressing this.
Question: In antiquity, the people comprised four groups: scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants. Outside these there were no other groups. Thus, when the four groups were settled and secure, all under Heaven was well governed. The emperors and kings of antiquity…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
未有不安此而稱治者然羲農十三卦
之制耒耜教耕以興農日中為市以通
商何不及於士工虞九官之命稷播穀
垂共工何不及於士商周禮太宰八則
有馭士者矣農工商其無馭乎太宰九
職列農工商矣而士獨安所職乎其曰
馭曰職者可悉數之歟管子謂昔聖王
處四民使士就燕閒工就官府商就市
井農就田野而不雜故士農之子常為
===
士農工商之子常為工商而不遷然伊
尹處畎畝膠鬲販魚鹽果不雜乎欒胥
之後在皂楚相之子負薪果不遷乎降
及後世雜與遷甚矣韓子謂今之為民
者六余謂今之為民者七游手其一也
今之三民興而四民病矣欲盡驅其三
以合乎四可乎凡士之游校者送迎奪
業衣食困心入官者待闕苦久資格苦
拘工之上京者艱於客資居家者疲於
punctuated: 未有不安此而稱治者。然羲農十三卦之制，耒耜教耕以興農，日中為市以通商，何不及於士工？虞九官之命，稷播穀，垂共工，何不及於士商？周禮太宰八則，有馭士者矣，農工商其無馭乎？太宰九職，列農工商矣，而士獨安所職乎？其曰馭曰職者，可悉數之歟？管子謂昔聖王處四民，使士就燕閒，工就官府，商就市井，農就田野，而不雜，故士農之子常為士農，工商之子常為工商，而不遷。然伊尹處畎畝，膠鬲販魚鹽，果不雜乎？欒胥之後在皂，楚相之子負薪，果不遷乎？降及後世，雜與遷甚矣。韓子謂今之為民者六，余謂今之為民者七，游手其一也。今之三民興而四民病矣，欲盡驅其三以合乎四，可乎？凡士之游校者，送迎奪業，衣食困心；入官者，待闕苦久，資格苦拘。工之上京者，艱於客資；居家者，疲於
translation_en:
…none ever claimed to have achieved good government without bringing security to these four groups. Yet among the institutions associated with the thirteen hexagrams of Fuxi and Shennong, plows and plowshares were used to teach cultivation and promote agriculture, and markets were held at midday to facilitate commerce. Why did these not extend to scholars and artisans? In the appointments of the nine officials under Shun, Ji was charged with sowing grain and Chui with overseeing artisans. Why did these not extend to scholars and merchants? Among the eight principles of the Grand Steward in the Rites of Zhou, there were provisions for governing officers. Were there none for governing farmers, artisans, and merchants? The Grand Steward’s nine occupations included farming, crafts, and commerce; what occupation, then, was assigned to scholars alone? Can you enumerate fully what are called the principles of governance and the occupations?

The Guanzi says that the sage kings of old settled the four groups of people by placing scholars in quiet retirement, artisans in government establishments, merchants in marketplaces, and farmers in the fields, keeping them from intermingling. Thus the sons of scholars and farmers always remained scholars and farmers, and the sons of artisans and merchants always remained artisans and merchants, without changing their occupations. Yet Yi Yin lived among the fields, and Jiao Ge traded in fish and salt: was there really no intermingling? The descendants of Luan and Xu served as grooms, and the son of a chief minister of Chu carried firewood: was there really no change? In later ages, intermingling and changes of occupation became extensive. Master Han said that in his day there were six groups of people; I say that today there are seven, idle people being one of them. Today the three additional groups flourish while the four original groups suffer. Would it be possible to compel all of those three groups to join the four?

Among scholars attending schools, ceremonial send-offs and receptions interrupt their studies, while clothing and food weigh upon their minds. Those entering official service suffer from long waits for vacancies and the restrictions imposed by eligibility requirements. Artisans who travel to the capital struggle to meet the expenses of living away from home; those who remain at home are worn out by…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
官役商之營大利者為勢豪所侵務小
本者為征徭所窘是三者皆病也而未
有甚於農者耕耨正忙而召役者呌囂
其室麥禾未熟而徵租者鞭撻其膚故
雖力耕疾織而樂歲有凍餒凶年有流
亡也病不已甚乎而士者或玩愒不學
浮華無實農者或惰而不力富而不節
工者或作巧技以眩俗為苦器以誤人
商者或表美售惡務奢逞慾又皆自病
===
者此在往古治世亦往往有之而未始
不處之也今承平百年超邁往古蓋已
無此矣萬一有之可不為之處乎願聞
所以處之之道
問學猶殖也不學將落故君子不可一日
而無學也然自正學不傳知學者鮮學
豈易言哉三滅之書上聖猶學也一善
之服大賢猶學也彼有通達國體可方
伊管何云其不善學潜心大業為世儒
punctuated:
官役。商之營大利者，為勢豪所侵；務小本者，為征徭所窘。是三者皆病也，而未有甚於農者。耕耨正忙，而召役者呌囂其室；麥禾未熟，而徵租者鞭撻其膚。故雖力耕疾織，而樂歲有凍餒，凶年有流亡也。病不已甚乎？而士者或玩愒不學，浮華無實；農者或惰而不力，富而不節；工者或作巧技以眩俗，為苦器以誤人；商者或表美售惡，務奢逞慾，又皆自病者。此在往古治世，亦往往有之，而未始不處之也。今承平百年，超邁往古，蓋已無此矣。萬一有之，可不為之處乎？願聞所以處之之道。

問：學猶殖也，不學將落，故君子不可一日而無學也。然自正學不傳，知學者鮮，學豈易言哉？三滅之書，上聖猶學也；一善之服，大賢猶學也。彼有通達國體，可方伊管，何云其不善學？潜心大業，為世儒
translation_en:
…government service obligations. Among merchants, those pursuing large profits suffer encroachment by powerful local magnates, while those trading with small amounts of capital are constrained by levies and service obligations. These three groups all suffer hardship, yet none suffers more than the farmers. Just when plowing and hoeing are most pressing, those summoning them for service shout at their homes; before the wheat and grain have ripened, tax collectors lash their bodies. Thus, though they plow strenuously and weave diligently, even in good harvest years some freeze and starve, while in bad years some flee their homes. Is their suffering not already extreme? Yet some scholars idle away their time without studying, displaying superficial brilliance without substance; some farmers are lazy and exert no effort, or become wealthy but exercise no restraint; some artisans devise ingenious contrivances to dazzle ordinary people and make defective utensils [?] to deceive others; and some merchants offer attractive exteriors while selling inferior goods, pursuing extravagance and indulging their desires. All these also bring hardship upon themselves. Such things often occurred even in the well-governed ages of antiquity, but they were never left unaddressed. Now we have enjoyed a hundred years of peace, surpassing antiquity, and presumably such things no longer exist. But should they happen to occur, could we leave them unaddressed? We wish to hear how they should be dealt with.

Question: Learning is like cultivation: without learning, one will decline. Thus the gentleman cannot go a single day without learning. Yet since the orthodox learning ceased to be transmitted, few have understood learning. Can learning readily be discussed? Even the highest sage studied a book described as “thrice obliterated” [?]; even the great worthy learned through “submission to a single good quality” [?]. There was one who thoroughly understood the principles of governing the state and could be compared to Yi Yin and Guan Zhong: why was he said not to be good at learning? Another devoted himself to the great undertaking and was, among the Confucian scholars of his age …

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
宗何云其不窺大道或尊大王室或處
死不亂或精明博洽或朴厚端重而曷
為蒙不學之譏或明習漢制或經術通
明或文學絶倫或藻警得幸而曷為致
不識字之誚以六經之文為諸儒倡而
何以用世之學不如人以古文之任為
天下師而何以本領之學不如人倡絶
學於孔孟而不欲以一善成名何以中
年而尚不及顏閔之徒集大成於諸儒
===
而力以斯文為已任何以晚歲而猶有
義理無窮之嘆處都城俗學之中而卒
究大業其學何事乎出黨禁偽學之後
而能明正道其道何傳乎夫士有好學
之志必其有尚友之心易曰多識前言
往行以畜其德是矣何先正有玩物喪
志之戒傳曰學優而仕仕優而學是矣
何說者有學而後從政未聞以政為學
之言古之學者有四失今欲去之何由
punctuated: 宗，何云其不窺大道？或尊大王室，或處死不亂，或精明博洽，或朴厚端重，而曷為蒙不學之譏？或明習漢制，或經術通明，或文學絶倫，或藻警得幸，而曷為致不識字之誚？以六經之文為諸儒倡，而何以用世之學不如人？以古文之任為天下師，而何以本領之學不如人？倡絶學於孔孟，而不欲以一善成名，何以中年而尚不及顏閔之徒？集大成於諸儒，而力以斯文為已任，何以晚歲而猶有義理無窮之嘆？處都城俗學之中，而卒究大業，其學何事乎？出黨禁偽學之後，而能明正道，其道何傳乎？夫士有好學之志，必其有尚友之心。《易》曰：「多識前言往行，以畜其德。」是矣，何先正有玩物喪志之戒？《傳》曰：「學優而仕，仕優而學。」是矣，何說者有「學而後從政，未聞以政為學」之言？古之學者有四失，今欲去之，何由？
translation_en:
…a paragon for scholars—why was he said not to have glimpsed the Great Way? Some upheld the royal house’s dignity; some faced death without losing composure; some were discerning and widely learned; some were sincere, generous, dignified, and grave. Why, then, were they reproached as unlearned? Some thoroughly understood Han institutions; some clearly comprehended classical learning; some were unrivaled in literary accomplishment; some gained favor through striking literary expression. Why, then, were they mocked as unable to read? One led the scholars through his writings on the Six Classics: why was his learning for practical service to the world inferior to that of others? One took responsibility for ancient-style prose and became a teacher to all under Heaven: why was his learning in fundamental matters inferior to that of others? One championed the interrupted tradition of learning from Confucius and Mencius and did not wish to win renown through a single good quality: why, even in middle age, had he still not equaled the likes of Yan Hui and Min Sun? One brought the learning of the various scholars to its fullest synthesis and devoted himself to carrying forward this cultural tradition: why, in his later years, did he still sigh over the inexhaustibility of moral principles? One lived amid the conventional learning of the capital yet ultimately mastered the great undertaking: what did his learning concern? One emerged after the partisan prohibitions against so-called false learning and was able to elucidate the correct Way: what transmission did his Way derive from?

A scholar determined to love learning must surely have the desire to befriend the worthy of antiquity. The Book of Changes says, “Acquaint yourself widely with the words and deeds of the past, thereby nurturing your virtue.” This is right; why, then, did a former worthy warn that preoccupation with things undermines one’s resolve? The transmitted text says, “When learning leaves strength to spare, take office; when office leaves strength to spare, study.” This is right; why, then, did a commentator say, “Study before undertaking government; I have never heard of using government as a means of learning”? Learners of antiquity had four failings. By what means might we now eliminate them?

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
今之學者有三岐古能一之何道方今
教養無異道術業有專攻是宜正學日
隆陋前修而弗之齒矣然有以明經規
進取而束書於釋蹻之餘以吏事為才
諝而喪志於敭歷之久俾儒者之功不
大見於世也亦何有於士哉夫學官先
事士先志今言不及於數而叩將以盡
其大鳴也盍各言其志乎
問古之論為政者亦多術矣而大要不過
===
曰振士風戢吏治阜民財飭邊備而已
天下之治誠不外此深求其故若不皆
然何也漢元光之初崇尚儒術表章六
經爰致文學大興而學士經生迭入為
相士風可謂振矣何以公卿多保位之
人而無補漢政之不綱歟建武之世嚴
察職事屢易守長而數世之後屏黜貪
污天下肅然吏治戢矣何以朝野有三
空之語而卒致炎綱之日弛與唐貞觀
punctuated:
今之學者有三岐，古能一之何道？方今教養無異道，術業有專攻，是宜正學日隆，陋前修而弗之齒矣。然有以明經規進取，而束書於釋蹻之餘；以吏事為才諝，而喪志於敭歷之久，俾儒者之功不大見於世也，亦何有於士哉？夫學官先事，士先志。今言不及於數，而叩將以盡其大鳴也，盍各言其志乎？

問：古之論為政者亦多術矣，而大要不過曰振士風、戢吏治、阜民財、飭邊備而已。天下之治誠不外此，深求其故，若不皆然，何也？漢元光之初，崇尚儒術，表章六經，爰致文學大興，而學士經生迭入為相，士風可謂振矣。何以公卿多保位之人，而無補漢政之不綱歟？建武之世，嚴察職事，屢易守長，而數世之後，屏黜貪污，天下肅然，吏治戢矣。何以朝野有三空之語，而卒致炎綱之日弛與？唐貞觀
translation_en:
Scholars today follow three divergent paths: by what Way did the ancients bring them into unity? Today, instruction and nurture follow a common Way, while scholarly pursuits have their particular specializations. Orthodox learning ought therefore to flourish daily, making earlier worthies seem so inadequate as scarcely to merit comparison. Yet some use mastery of the Classics to seek advancement, only to bundle away their books after taking off their straw sandals to enter office. They regard skill in administrative affairs as talent and discernment, but lose their aspirations during long service in successive posts. Thus the achievements of Confucian scholars do not become greatly manifest in the world. What, then, remains of their claim to be scholars? In learning for office, practical affairs come first; for a scholar, aspiration comes first. My questions here do not extend to particulars [?]; rather, by striking the bell, I seek to draw forth its fullest resonance. Why not each state your aspirations?

Question: The ancients who discussed government proposed many methods, yet their essentials amounted to no more than invigorating the ethos of scholars, disciplining the administration of officials, increasing the people's wealth, and putting frontier defenses in order. The government of the realm indeed falls within these concerns; yet, when we inquire deeply into the reasons, matters seem not always to have worked this way. Why?

At the beginning of the Han Yuanguang era, Confucian learning was exalted and the Six Classics were honored and promoted. Classical scholarship consequently flourished, and learned men and specialists in the Classics entered office in succession as chief ministers. The ethos of scholars could indeed be called invigorated. Why, then, were the highest officials mostly men intent on preserving their positions, who did nothing to remedy the disorder of Han government?

During the Jianwu era, the performance of official duties was rigorously scrutinized, and commandery and county heads were repeatedly replaced. Several reigns later, the greedy and corrupt were dismissed, and the whole realm stood in awed obedience: official administration had been brought under discipline. Why, then, was there talk at court and in the countryside of the ‘three depletions,’ and why did the governing order of the Han dynasty ultimately grow laxer by the day? In the Tang Zhenguan era …

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之末斗米三錢外戶不閉幾致刑措號
稱太平民財可謂阜矣而閭閻多怨讟
之言不若貞觀初年饑饉相仍而民無
愁苦何歟宋熙寧之間剙立保甲增修
戍壘熙河闢壤高麗来庭而不免啓釁
之端不及祖宗歷世武略雖微而仁澤
深厚何歟凡若此者或病其用舍失宜
或咎其刑罰不中或言其驕侈之漸或
議其聽斷之偏不知四者之弊於彼四
===
事何所關歟抑别有其由而不繫於此
歟若夫賢才彙進而士風日汚按劾不
遺而吏治益雜催科與恤典並舉民生
何自而安羽書與捷報交馳邊備何時
而飭綜覈於四事之間孰為當捄之弊
探討於四事之外孰為尤務之宜攄紙
上之陳言發胷中之特見固儒者之能
事也然言必當理事必當務吾於諸生
望之矣
punctuated:
之末，斗米三錢，外戶不閉，幾致刑措，號稱太平，民財可謂阜矣。而閭閻多怨讟之言，不若貞觀初年饑饉相仍而民無愁苦，何歟？宋熙寧之間，剙立保甲，增修戍壘，熙河闢壤，高麗来庭，而不免啓釁之端，不及祖宗歷世武略雖微而仁澤深厚，何歟？凡若此者，或病其用舍失宜，或咎其刑罰不中，或言其驕侈之漸，或議其聽斷之偏。不知四者之弊，於彼四事何所關歟？抑别有其由，而不繫於此歟？
若夫賢才彙進而士風日汚，按劾不遺而吏治益雜，催科與恤典並舉，民生何自而安？羽書與捷報交馳，邊備何時而飭？綜覈於四事之間，孰為當捄之弊？探討於四事之外，孰為尤務之宜？攄紙上之陳言，發胷中之特見，固儒者之能事也。然言必當理，事必當務，吾於諸生望之矣。
translation_en:
…toward the end of the Zhenguan reign, a dou of rice cost three cash, outer doors were left unbarred, and punishments had almost fallen into disuse. The age was acclaimed as one of great peace, and the people's material resources could indeed be called abundant. Yet complaints and resentment were widespread among the common people. Why did this fall short of the early Zhenguan years, when famines followed one another but the people felt no distress or bitterness? During the Xining reign of the Song, the baojia system of mutual responsibility and militia organization was established, frontier fortifications were expanded and repaired, territory was opened up in Xihe, and Gaoli came to court. Yet these measures could not avoid sowing the seeds of conflict. Why did this fall short of the successive reigns of the founding and ancestral emperors, whose military achievements were modest but whose benevolence and beneficent influence were profound? In such cases, some find fault with inappropriate appointments and dismissals; some blame punishments that missed the proper measure; some speak of the gradual growth of arrogance and extravagance; and some criticize partiality in hearing and deciding affairs. How, then, are these four failings related to those four matters? Or were there other causes, unconnected with these?
Consider worthy and talented men advancing in great numbers while the moral character of scholars grows daily more corrupt, and investigations and impeachments allowing nothing to escape while official administration becomes increasingly disordered. When the pressing collection of taxes and measures of relief are pursued together, how can the people's livelihood become secure? When urgent military dispatches and reports of victory speed back and forth, when will frontier defenses be put in order? Examining these four matters comprehensively, which abuses ought to be remedied? Looking beyond these four matters, which appropriate measures most urgently demand attention? Setting forth received statements committed to paper and expressing distinctive insights from one's own mind are indeed tasks in which a Confucian scholar should excel. Yet one's words must accord with principle, and one's proposals must address the affairs that require attention. This is what I expect of you candidates.

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
問窮理盡性之餘而游心載籍以廣前聞
固君子所不廢也然代遠文繁言殽簡
錯不資博辨曷啓深懵沮誦造字書契
曷始於軒轅虞舜作韶六韶曷原於帝
嚳商湯問罪之師間道用升陘之計伊
尹耕莘之隱輕身為負鼎之要太公之
遇文王或云載自渭陽或謂歸於東海
微子之歸周室或言出遯荒野或曰抱
器軍門周世共和之號或以為二公共
===
和王政之義或以為共伯之名楚人椒
蘭之辭或以為二人悞君之名或以為
君子之喻曾子易簀而終何以見記禮
者之寓貶宰我從畔而及何以知作史
者之傳譌遷史稱四皓之翼儲通鑑何
疑而不載通鑑削屈平之自溺綱目何
取而見收以火禁原介子之燔則周人
有司燿之職以海濤乘子胥之怒則先
儒有随月之談凡傳聞之異疑諒折衷
punctuated: 問：窮理盡性之餘，而游心載籍以廣前聞，固君子所不廢也。然代遠文繁，言殽簡錯，不資博辨，曷啓深懵？沮誦造字，書契曷始於軒轅？虞舜作韶，六韶曷原於帝嚳？商湯問罪之師，間道用升陘之計；伊尹耕莘之隱，輕身為負鼎之要。太公之遇文王，或云載自渭陽，或謂歸於東海；微子之歸周室，或言出遯荒野，或曰抱器軍門。周世共和之號，或以為二公共和王政之義，或以為共伯之名。楚人椒蘭之辭，或以為二人悞君之名，或以為君子之喻。曾子易簀而終，何以見記禮者之寓貶？宰我從畔而及，何以知作史者之傳譌？遷史稱四皓之翼儲，《通鑑》何疑而不載？《通鑑》削屈平之自溺，《綱目》何取而見收？以火禁原介子之燔，則周人有司燿之職；以海濤乘子胥之怒，則先儒有随月之談。凡傳聞之異疑，諒折衷
translation_en:
Question: Beyond investigating principles to the utmost and fully realizing one’s nature, roaming in the written records to broaden one’s knowledge of the past is certainly something the gentleman does not neglect. Yet the ages are remote and the writings abundant; statements are confused and bamboo slips disordered. Without wide learning and discrimination, how can profound ignorance be dispelled? If Ju Song invented characters, why is writing said to have begun with Xuanyuan? If Yu Shun composed the Shao music, why are the Six Shao traced to Emperor Ku? When Shang Tang sent an army to punish wrongdoing, he employed the stratagem of taking a byroad through Shengxing; Yi Yin, living in retirement and farming at Shen, lowered himself to seek access by carrying a cooking tripod [?]. Of the Grand Duke’s encounter with King Wen, some say that he was brought back in the king’s carriage from the northern bank of the Wei River, while others say that he returned from the eastern sea. Of Weizi’s submission to the Zhou royal house, some say that he fled into the wilderness, while others say that he carried ritual vessels to the army’s gate.

As for the designation Gonghe in the Zhou era, some understand it to mean that the two dukes jointly brought harmony to royal government, while others take it to be the name of the Earl of Gong. As for the words jiao and lan—pepper and orchid—in the writings of the man of Chu, some take them as the names of two men who misled their ruler, while others regard them as metaphors for gentlemen. Zengzi changed his sleeping mat before dying: how can we discern an implicit censure by the recorder of the rites? Zai Wo joined a rebellion and was caught up in its consequences: how do we know that the historian transmitted an error? Sima Qian’s history praises the Four Hoary Elders for supporting the heir apparent: what doubts caused the Comprehensive Mirror to omit this? The Comprehensive Mirror deletes the account of Qu Ping’s drowning himself: on what grounds does the Outline and Details include it? If the prohibition on fire is traced to Jiezi’s death by burning, the Zhou people nevertheless had the office of Director of Fire. If the ocean’s waves are attributed to Zixu’s anger, earlier Confucian scholars nevertheless spoke of their following the moon. Concerning all these discrepancies and uncertainties in transmitted accounts, surely, in adjudicating among them …

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text: 之有要畧引其概佇聽洽聞
punctuated: 之有要，畧引其概，佇聽洽聞。
translation_en: …there are essential principles for adjudicating these matters. Briefly outline the main points; we await your broadly informed response.

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人一百三十五名
第一名白鉞直隸真定府南宮縣學生詩
第二名譚昇順天府平谷縣學生易
第三名尹頌順天府學增廣生書

text:
第壹場
四書
先事後得非崇德與
同考試官教諭程批此篇理明辭暢宜表而出之
同考試官教諭劉批作此題者多泛而不切是
篇辭理俱到超出衆作宜錄以示學者
考試官諭德陸批講崇德處尤緊峭讀之聳然
考試官侍講學士楊批理明辭健盖嘗用心於此者
===
惟務所當為不計所當獲此德所以日崇也夫
人惟有利欲之心故德不崇也苟惟務其所當
為而不計其所當獲則利欲之心亡矣德其有
不崇乎昔孔子因樊遲問崇德而告之以此盖
事務與功效而相承利欲與義理而相勝世未
有為其事而不得功效者然未為而巳計其功
方為而遽圖其效乃利欲之心而非義理也欲
崇德者必先其所當為之事而後其所當得之
功先者為之在先而無少慢後者置之在後而

第壹場
四書
先事後得，非崇德與？

惟務所當為，不計所當獲，此德所以日崇也。夫人惟有利欲之心，故德不崇也。苟惟務其所當為，而不計其所當獲，則利欲之心亡矣，德其有不崇乎？昔孔子因樊遲問崇德，而告之以此。盖事務與功效而相承，利欲與義理而相勝。世未有為其事而不得功效者，然未為而巳計其功，方為而遽圖其效，乃利欲之心，而非義理也。欲崇德者，必先其所當為之事，而後其所當得之功。先者，為之在先而無少慢；後者，置之在後而

First Session
Four Books

“To put the work first and its rewards afterward—is this not to exalt virtue?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: This essay’s reasoning is clear and its language fluent. It deserves to be singled out and published.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Most who write on this topic are vague and fail to address it precisely. This essay is accomplished in both expression and reasoning, surpassing the other compositions. It should be recorded for students to study.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Admonisher of Virtue: The discussion of exalting virtue is especially incisive and forceful. Reading it stirs one profoundly.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Academician Expositor-in-waiting: Clear reasoning and vigorous language: the writer must have devoted thought to this matter.

To attend solely to what one ought to do, without calculating what one ought to gain—this is how virtue grows loftier day by day. It is precisely because people harbor thoughts of profit and desire that their virtue does not rise. If they attend solely to what they ought to do, without calculating what they ought to gain, thoughts of profit and desire will disappear. How could their virtue then fail to rise? In former times, when Fan Chi asked about exalting virtue, Confucius instructed him with these words. Undertakings and their results follow upon one another, while profit and desire contend with righteousness and principle. Never has anyone carried out an undertaking without obtaining results. Yet to calculate its accomplishments before undertaking it, or hastily to seek its effects just as one begins, expresses a mind bent on profit and desire, rather than righteousness and principle. Those who wish to exalt virtue must put first the work they ought to do and place afterward the accomplishments they ought to obtain. text:
不復計無大無小之事為必先之而於其功一
皆後焉若常若變之事動輒先之而於其效亦
皆後焉夫如是德不以之而崇乎盖道得於心
之謂德一有利心則道之已得者亦日亡矣理
得於心之謂德一有欲心則道之未得者將終
失矣今既先其事而後其得則一行吾義而欲
心不萌德於是乎日積土自一簣而成九仞之
山者不足以喻之也一循吾理而利心不作德
於是乎日增木起尺寸而聳千尋之榦者不足
===
以方之也然則先事後得豈非崇德也與聖人
之言厥旨深矣抑考此章樊遲問崇德聖人既
以此告矣他日子張亦問崇德而聖人告之曰
主忠信徙義崇德也又與此異何歟盖樊遲麤
鄙近利不能循理去欲子張務外自高不能誠
善補過故告之異也天之生物因材而篤聖人
之教不猶是乎
辟如四時之錯行如日月之代明
punctuated:
不復計。無大無小之事，為必先之，而於其功，一皆後焉；若常若變之事，動輒先之，而於其效，亦皆後焉。夫如是，德不以之而崇乎？盖道得於心之謂德，一有利心，則道之已得者亦日亡矣；理得於心之謂德，一有欲心，則道之未得者將終失矣。今既先其事而後其得，則一行吾義而欲心不萌，德於是乎日積，土自一簣而成九仞之山者，不足以喻之也；一循吾理而利心不作，德於是乎日增，木起尺寸而聳千尋之榦者，不足以方之也。然則先事後得，豈非崇德也與？聖人之言，厥旨深矣！抑考此章，樊遲問崇德，聖人既以此告矣。他日，子張亦問崇德，而聖人告之曰：「主忠信，徙義，崇德也。」又與此異，何歟？盖樊遲麤鄙近利，不能循理去欲；子張務外自高，不能誠善補過，故告之異也。天之生物，因材而篤，聖人之教不猶是乎？

辟如四時之錯行，如日月之代明。
translation_en:
…and no longer reckon it. In matters great or small, one must put doing them first and leave all consideration of their results until afterward. In matters ordinary or exceptional, whenever one acts, one puts the task first and likewise leaves all consideration of its effects until afterward. In this way, will virtue not be exalted? For virtue means the Way apprehended in the heart. Once a desire for profit arises, even what one has already apprehended of the Way diminishes daily. Virtue means principle apprehended in the heart. Once a selfish desire arises, what one has not yet apprehended of the Way will ultimately be lost. Now, by putting the task first and its rewards afterward, one acts entirely according to righteousness, and selfish desire does not sprout. Virtue thus accumulates daily: even earth piled up from a single basketful into a mountain nine ren high is inadequate as an illustration. One follows principle alone, and the desire for profit does not arise. Virtue thus increases daily: even a tree growing from an inch or a foot into a trunk towering a thousand xun is inadequate as a comparison. Is putting the task first and its rewards afterward, then, not the exaltation of virtue? How profound is the meaning of the sage’s words!

Yet consider this chapter: when Fan Chi asked about exalting virtue, the sage instructed him in these terms. On another day, Zizhang also asked about exalting virtue, and the sage told him: “Make loyalty and trustworthiness your guiding principles, and move toward righteousness: this is to exalt virtue.” Why does this differ from the present teaching? Fan Chi was coarse and uncultivated, inclined toward profit, and unable to follow principle and eliminate selfish desire. Zizhang devoted himself to outward appearances and thought highly of himself; he could not make his goodness sincere and remedy his faults. Thus the instructions given to them differed. When Heaven brings things into being, it nurtures them according to their inherent capacities. Is the sage’s teaching not just like this?

“It is like the four seasons proceeding in succession, like the sun and moon shining in turn.”

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導謝批士子於燈窓閣筆此題久矣
場中能此沛然理無破綻眾人不足子乃有餘竒哉
同考試官學正陳批黏上文則太泥駕空又泛然
理學之難言也觀此知製錦者之別有機矣
考試官諭德陸批文有精采說理者所難也
考試官侍講學士楊批形容聖德辭意俱新佳作也
中庸擬聖德之無窮猶天道之無息也盖聖人
之德即天道也中庸欲明聖德之無窮使不擬
諸天道之無息其何以形容之哉中庸三十章
===
欲以聖人之德而明天道先以天道而擬聖人
之德若曰吾夫子以天縱之資上聖之德集四
聖之大成參兩間之妙用若其用舍行藏隨寓
而安無可無不可也仕止久速各當其可無過
無不及也其變通也用之無方體其盛大也出
之無終窮故欲言其德之昭著也而有渾淪者
存言其德之渾淪也而有悠久者具盖天即聖
人也辟諸天道其猶四時之迭運乎自春而夏
倏秋而冬二氣之行若紛然而不齊矣不知寒
punctuated:
同考試官訓導謝批：士子於燈窓閣筆此題久矣，場中能此沛然，理無破綻，眾人不足，子乃有餘，竒哉！

同考試官學正陳批：黏上文則太泥，駕空又泛然，理學之難言也！觀此，知製錦者之別有機矣。

考試官諭德陸批：文有精采，說理者所難也。

考試官侍講學士楊批：形容聖德，辭意俱新，佳作也。

中庸擬聖德之無窮，猶天道之無息也。盖聖人之德即天道也，中庸欲明聖德之無窮，使不擬諸天道之無息，其何以形容之哉？中庸三十章欲以聖人之德而明天道，先以天道而擬聖人之德。若曰：吾夫子以天縱之資、上聖之德，集四聖之大成，參兩間之妙用。若其用舍行藏，隨寓而安，無可無不可也；仕止久速，各當其可，無過無不及也。其變通也，用之無方體；其盛大也，出之無終窮。故欲言其德之昭著也，而有渾淪者存；言其德之渾淪也，而有悠久者具。盖天即聖人也，辟諸天道，其猶四時之迭運乎？自春而夏，倏秋而冬，二氣之行，若紛然而不齊矣，不知寒
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Xie, Assistant Instructor, comments: Students have long laid down their brushes before this topic at their lamplit windows. To produce such a flowing treatment in the examination hall, with no flaws in its reasoning—where others fall short, you have more than enough. Remarkable!

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: Clinging to the preceding passage makes the treatment too constrained; proceeding without a textual footing makes it vague. How difficult it is to discuss the learning of principle! Reading this, one realizes that the weaver of brocade has a special loom of his own.

Examiner Lu, Mentor, comments: The writing has brilliance, something difficult to achieve when expounding principle.

Examiner Yang, Expositor-in-waiting, comments: In depicting the sage’s virtue, both the wording and the ideas are fresh. An excellent composition.

The Doctrine of the Mean compares the inexhaustibility of the sage’s virtue to the ceaselessness of the Way of Heaven. For the sage’s virtue is itself the Way of Heaven. If the Doctrine of the Mean wished to illuminate the inexhaustibility of the sage’s virtue without comparing it to the ceaselessness of the Way of Heaven, how could it describe it? Chapter Thirty of the Doctrine of the Mean seeks to illuminate the Way of Heaven through the sage’s virtue, first using the Way of Heaven as an analogy for that virtue. It is as though it said: Our Master, with his Heaven-endowed gifts and the virtue of a supreme sage, brought together the consummate achievements of the four sages and participated in the wondrous workings between Heaven and Earth. Whether employed or set aside, coming forward or remaining in retirement, he was at ease wherever he found himself, neither insisting upon nor ruling out any course. Taking office or withdrawing, remaining long or departing quickly, he acted appropriately in each case, neither going too far nor falling short. In his adaptability, his practice had no fixed direction or form; in his grandeur, what he brought forth was inexhaustible. Thus, when one wishes to speak of the manifest radiance of his virtue, an undivided wholeness remains within it; when one speaks of its undivided wholeness, enduring constancy is also present. For Heaven is the sage himself. To compare him to the Way of Heaven, is he not like the successive movement of the four seasons? From spring to summer, suddenly autumn and then winter: the movements of the two vital forces seem confused and irregular, without one realizing that the cold …

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
暑推遷而嵗功於是乎成焉聖人即天也辟諸
天道其猶日月之更明乎方晝而夜忽望而朔
二曜之運若雜然而無序矣不知陰陽往来而
天道於是乎位焉是則天道之無息者如此聖
人之德無窮者亦如此一時中之道也中庸言
天道言聖德必以二者交相明之豈非善言聖
人者與抑考中庸此章及後二章皆以聖人之
德明天道也故此章但言天道之大而見聖人
之大後二章但言聖人之德而見天道之大然
===
天不能載地不能覆日明乎晝月明乎夜各得
陰陽之偏若吾夫子之德則得其全矣是夫子
大而天地小也此又深於理者之論因併及之
人心之所同然者何也謂理也義也聖人
先得我心之所同然耳故理義之悅我
心猶芻豢之悅我口
同考試官教諭馮批人心同然所以明降才之同
也此作得之表出以示學者
punctuated:
暑推遷，而嵗功於是乎成焉。聖人即天也，辟諸天道，其猶日月之更明乎？方晝而夜，忽望而朔，二曜之運若雜然而無序矣，不知陰陽往来，而天道於是乎位焉。是則天道之無息者如此，聖人之德無窮者亦如此，一時中之道也。《中庸》言天道、言聖德，必以二者交相明之，豈非善言聖人者與？抑考《中庸》此章及後二章，皆以聖人之德明天道也。故此章但言天道之大，而見聖人之大；後二章但言聖人之德，而見天道之大。然天不能載，地不能覆，日明乎晝，月明乎夜，各得陰陽之偏。若吾夫子之德，則得其全矣。是夫子大而天地小也。此又深於理者之論，因併及之。

人心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。故理義之悅我心，猶芻豢之悅我口。

同考試官教諭馮批：「人心同然，所以明降才之同也。此作得之，表出以示學者。」
translation_en:
…heat succeed one another, and thus the work of the year is accomplished. The sage is Heaven itself. To draw an analogy with the Way of Heaven, is this not like the sun and moon taking turns to shine? Day gives way to night; suddenly the full moon gives way to the new. The movements of the two luminaries seem confused and without sequence, yet one fails to recognize that through the coming and going of yin and yang, the Way of Heaven thereby assumes its proper order. Such is the ceaselessness of the Way of Heaven; such, too, is the inexhaustibility of the sage’s virtue. Both are the single Way of attaining the mean as circumstances require. When the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Way of Heaven and the virtue of the sage, it invariably uses each to illuminate the other. Is this not skillful discourse on the sage? Moreover, examining this chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean and the following two chapters, all use the sage’s virtue to illuminate the Way of Heaven. Thus this chapter speaks only of the greatness of the Way of Heaven, revealing the greatness of the sage; the following two chapters speak only of the sage’s virtue, revealing the greatness of the Way of Heaven. Yet Heaven cannot bear things up, and Earth cannot cover them; the sun shines by day, and the moon by night. Each possesses only one aspect of yin and yang. The virtue of our Master, however, possesses their entirety. Thus the Master is great, while Heaven and Earth are small. This, moreover, is the argument of those with a profound understanding of principle, and so I mention it here as well.

What is it that human hearts alike approve? It is principle and rightness. The sage has merely apprehended before us what our hearts alike approve. Thus principle and rightness delight my heart just as the meat of grass-fed and grain-fed animals delights my palate.

Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: “That human hearts alike approve the same things serves to clarify that the capacities bestowed by Heaven are the same. This composition grasps that point. I single it out to show students.”

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正陳批文有精神盖熟於孟子者
也非淺學所到庸表而出之
考試官諭德陸批辭不費而理自足可錄也
考試官侍講學士楊批玄酒無味此作類之
惟人心之然理義也同故人心之悅理義也至
盖理義人心之所同然也然之斯悅之矣然之
者雖聖人而亦同則悅之者豈不猶悅芻豢之
至哉今夫人之口鼻耳目皆有所同好而其心
獨無所同然乎心之所同然者何也謂在物之
===
理若父子之親君臣之義人孰不然之乎謂處
物之義若父子而親君臣而義人孰不可之乎
理固人心所同然也雖生知安行之聖人亦惟
先得乎此理而非有以異於人焉義亦人心所
同然也雖道全德備之聖人亦惟先覺乎此義
而非有以殊於衆焉人心之然理義信乎同矣
故我得乎理則人莫不以為美而吾之心怡然
悅懌而不知其手之舞真猶牛羊之味悅我口
矣我得乎義則人莫不以為善而吾之心懽然
punctuated:
同考試官學正陳批：文有精神，盖熟於孟子者也，非淺學所到，庸表而出之。
考試官諭德陸批：辭不費而理自足，可錄也。
考試官侍講學士楊批：玄酒無味，此作類之。
惟人心之然理義也同，故人心之悅理義也至。盖理義，人心之所同然也。然之斯悅之矣。然之者雖聖人而亦同，則悅之者豈不猶悅芻豢之至哉？今夫人之口鼻耳目皆有所同好，而其心獨無所同然乎？心之所同然者何也？謂在物之理，若父子之親、君臣之義，人孰不然之乎？謂處物之義，若父子而親、君臣而義，人孰不可之乎？理固人心所同然也，雖生知安行之聖人，亦惟先得乎此理，而非有以異於人焉。義亦人心所同然也，雖道全德備之聖人，亦惟先覺乎此義，而非有以殊於衆焉。人心之然理義，信乎同矣。故我得乎理，則人莫不以為美，而吾之心怡然悅懌，而不知其手之舞，真猶牛羊之味悅我口矣。我得乎義，則人莫不以為善，而吾之心懽然
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, an Instructor, comments: “The composition has vitality. Its author is surely well versed in the Mengzi; this is beyond the reach of shallow learning. Accordingly, we single it out for presentation.”
Examiner Lu, an Admonisher of Virtue, comments: “The language is economical, yet the reasoning is complete in itself. It merits inclusion.”
Examiner Yang, a Hanlin Expositor-in-waiting, comments: “The dark wine—the water used in sacrifice—has no flavor; this composition resembles it.”
Precisely because human hearts alike assent to principle and rightness, their delight in principle and rightness is profound. Principle and rightness are what human hearts alike affirm. To affirm them is thus to delight in them. Even sages share this same affirmation; must not the delight in them therefore be as profound as the delight in grass-fed and grain-fed meats? Now, people’s mouths, noses, ears, and eyes all have preferences in common. Could their hearts alone have nothing that they alike affirm? What is it that their hearts alike affirm? It is the principle inherent in things: who does not affirm such things as affection between father and son and rightness between ruler and minister? It is rightness in dealing with things: who does not approve of father and son acting with affection, and ruler and minister acting with rightness?
Principle is indeed what human hearts alike affirm. Even sages who possess knowledge from birth and act rightly with ease merely apprehend this principle before others; they have nothing in this respect that sets them apart from other people. Rightness too is what human hearts alike affirm. Even sages in whom the Way is whole and virtue complete merely awaken to this rightness before others; they have nothing in this respect that distinguishes them from the multitude. Human hearts truly are alike in affirming principle and rightness.
Thus, when I attain principle, everyone regards it as admirable, and my heart is so contented and delighted that, without my knowing it, my hands dance. Truly, it is like the flavor of beef and mutton delighting my mouth. When I attain rightness, everyone regards it as good, and my heart joyfully…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
喜樂而不知其足之蹈誠若犬豕之味悅我口
矣人心之悅理義不亦至乎夫理義性也人心
之於理義然之如彼其同悅之若此其至人性
之善豈不信哉嗟乎世至戰國聖賢不作理義
不明人不復知其性之本善而以聖人不可及
也孟子欲救其弊故其見滕世子也嘗道性善
稱堯舜而此與前數章反覆論辨皆以明人性
之本善聖人之可及使人復其本性而至於聖
人也先儒謂其有大功於世不以此歟
===
易
大君之宜行中之謂也
同考試官教諭程 批 行中便是大君之宜作者
多不識故皆辭浮理舛惟此篇認理真切而辭足以發之
矧他篇俱純擢之以冠本房
同考試官教諭劉 批 題本明白簡約或以大君之
宜本於行中是未達之謂之意或以為用九六之剛中不知五
自居中惟此作體認切當措辭雄贍出人意表故錄之
punctuated:
喜樂而不知其足之蹈，誠若犬豕之味悅我口矣。人心之悅理義，不亦至乎？夫理義，性也。人心之於理義，然之如彼其同，悅之若此其至，人性之善豈不信哉？嗟乎！世至戰國，聖賢不作，理義不明，人不復知其性之本善，而以聖人不可及也。孟子欲救其弊，故其見滕世子也，嘗道性善，稱堯舜，而此與前數章反覆論辨，皆以明人性之本善、聖人之可及，使人復其本性而至於聖人也。先儒謂其有大功於世，不以此歟？

易
大君之宜，行中之謂也。

同考試官教諭程批：行中便是大君之宜，作者多不識，故皆辭浮理舛。惟此篇認理真切，而辭足以發之，矧他篇俱純，擢之以冠本房。

同考試官教諭劉批：題本明白簡約，或以大君之宜本於行中，是未達之謂之意；或以為用九六之剛中，不知五自居中。惟此作體認切當，措辭雄贍，出人意表，故錄之。
translation_en:
…joyful and happy, unaware that my feet are dancing: it is truly as though the taste of dog and pork were pleasing my palate. Is not the human heart’s delight in principle and righteousness complete? Principle and righteousness constitute our nature. Since human hearts agree so fully in affirming them and delight in them so completely, can the goodness of human nature be doubted? Alas! By the Warring States period, sages and worthies no longer arose, and principle and righteousness were no longer clearly understood. People no longer knew that their nature was originally good and considered sagehood beyond their reach. Mencius wished to remedy this failing. Thus, when he met the heir apparent of Teng, he spoke of the goodness of human nature and praised Yao and Shun. His repeated arguments in this and the preceding several chapters all clarify that human nature is originally good and that sagehood is attainable, enabling people to recover their original nature and become sages. Is this not why earlier Confucian scholars said that he had rendered a great service to the world?

Book of Changes
“What is fitting for a great ruler” refers to putting the mean into practice.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: Putting the mean into practice is precisely what is fitting for a great ruler. Most candidates fail to understand this, so their language is superficial and their reasoning mistaken. This essay alone grasps the principle truly and precisely, and its language adequately expresses it. Moreover, the candidate’s other essays are all sound. I have promoted it to first place in this examining section.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: The topic is clear and concise. Some take what is fitting for a great ruler to be based upon putting the mean into practice; this fails to grasp the sense of “refers to.” Others take it to mean employing the firm centrality of the nine and six [?], unaware that the fifth line itself occupies the central position. This composition alone comprehends the meaning precisely and fittingly; its language is forceful and ample, surpassing expectations. I have therefore selected it for inclusion.

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官諭德陸批〔理致超詣易學之粹然者〕
考試官侍講學士楊批〔發明行中之旨甚當〕
論得居尊之所利者即其行至道而為言也夫
道以中為至臨六五得大君之宜者是即行此
至道而已豈有他謂哉昔孔子釋周公臨六五
之爻辭如此盖六五居尊下應九二能不自任
而任臣取天下之善以臨民是大君之所利也
不自用而用賢合天下之知以涖衆是大君之
所宜也爻辭之旨如此不過行中之謂耳盖五
===
居上體之中有中之義為大君者若汶汶焉不
知任賢而乏人以為輔則不及乎中矣若訑訑
然不肯用人而任察以為明則太過乎中矣惟
六五克知任賢而善盖乎天下未始有不及之
患是以行乎中道而凡臨民之事若教思无窮
若容保无疆者无往而非中也獨能用人而智
周乎萬物未始有太過之弊是能得乎中行而
凡涖衆之道與坤地同厚與兌澤同深者无適
而非中也夫道不中則事不宜惟中所以宜也
punctuated:
考試官諭德陸批〔理致超詣，易學之粹然者。〕
考試官侍講學士楊批〔發明行中之旨甚當。〕
論得居尊之所利者，即其行至道而為言也。夫道以中為至，臨六五得大君之宜者，是即行此至道而已，豈有他謂哉？昔孔子釋周公臨六五之爻辭如此。盖六五居尊，下應九二，能不自任而任臣，取天下之善以臨民，是大君之所利也；不自用而用賢，合天下之知以涖衆，是大君之所宜也。爻辭之旨如此，不過行中之謂耳。盖五居上體之中，有中之義。為大君者，若汶汶焉不知任賢，而乏人以為輔，則不及乎中矣；若訑訑然不肯用人，而任察以為明，則太過乎中矣。惟六五克知任賢，而善盖乎天下，未始有不及之患，是以行乎中道，而凡臨民之事，若教思无窮，若容保无疆者，无往而非中也。獨能用人，而智周乎萬物，未始有太過之弊，是能得乎中行，而凡涖衆之道，與坤地同厚，與兌澤同深者，无適而非中也。夫道不中則事不宜，惟中所以宜也。

Comment by Examiner Lu, Admonisher: 〔The reasoning attains exceptional heights: this is a work of pure scholarship on the Book of Changes.〕
Comment by Examiner Yang, Academician Expositor-in-Waiting: 〔It elucidates most aptly the meaning of practicing the mean.〕
I submit that attaining what is beneficial to one occupying the exalted position is spoken of in terms of his practicing the highest Way. Now, the Way has the mean as its highest attainment. That the six in the fifth place of the hexagram Lin (Approach) attains what is fitting for a great ruler means simply that he practices this highest Way. What else could it mean? Such was Confucius’s explanation of the Duke of Zhou’s line statement for the six in the fifth place of Lin. This line occupies the exalted position and corresponds below to the nine in the second place. Able to entrust responsibility to ministers rather than assume it all himself, the ruler draws upon the goodness of all under Heaven to govern the people: this is what benefits a great ruler. Employing worthy men rather than relying on himself alone, he brings together the wisdom of all under Heaven to preside over the multitude: this is what is fitting for a great ruler. Such is the purport of the line statement; it means nothing more than practicing the mean.
The fifth place occupies the center of the upper trigram and thus carries the meaning of centrality. If a great ruler is so benighted that he does not know to entrust responsibility to worthy men, and consequently lacks people to assist him, he falls short of the mean. If he is so self-satisfied that he refuses to employ others, taking probing scrutiny for discernment, he exceeds the mean. The six in the fifth place, however, knows how to entrust responsibility to worthy men, so that goodness extends throughout all under Heaven, without ever suffering from deficiency. Thus he practices the Way of the mean, and in all matters of governing the people—whether thinking endlessly of their instruction or embracing and protecting them without bounds—there is nothing that does not accord with the mean. He is uniquely able to employ others, so that his wisdom encompasses the myriad things, without ever suffering from excess. Thus he attains conduct in accordance with the mean, and all his ways of presiding over the multitude, as substantial as the earth of Kun and as deep as the marsh of Dui, accord with the mean in every instance. If the Way does not accord with the mean, affairs will not be fitting. It is precisely the mean that makes them fitting.

…Then does what befits a great ruler not mean acting in accordance with the mean? Considered together, wise overseeing is precisely what befits a great ruler, and what befits a great ruler means acting in accordance with the mean. Wisdom, fittingness, and the mean differ in name but are identical in substance: distinguished, they are three; united, they are one. title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
專直故質无不包而大生坤既翕闢故量无不
容而廣生此易之所以廣大也歟盖嘗論之易
之道廣矣大矣而其所以廣大者則在乾坤焉
夫乾純陽至健其象為天一而實者也當其秋
冬之時體與坤别固其靈根是為靜矣其靜也
固之專壹而不雜此一之存也及其春夏之時
用與坤交播其群品是為動矣其動也播之正
直而不屈此一之達也惟一而實故其質渾淪
无外舉地之形无不包大可見矣此乾以靜專
===
動直而大生也易之所以大者以此夫坤純陰
至順其象為地二而虚者也當其利貞之際體
與乾别斂其元化是為靜矣其靜也斂之翕聚
而無遺此二之合也及乎元亨之際發其生意
是為動矣其動也發之開闢而无限此二之分
也惟二而虚故其量宏闊无疆盡天之氣无不
容廣可知矣是坤以靜翕動闢而廣生也易之
所以廣者以此抑攷此章上文言易廣矣大矣
此言乾大生坤廣生而下文遂言廣大配天地
punctuated: 專直，故質无不包而大生；坤既翕闢，故量无不容而廣生。此易之所以廣大也歟！盖嘗論之：易之道廣矣，大矣，而其所以廣大者，則在乾坤焉。夫乾純陽至健，其象為天，一而實者也。當其秋冬之時，體與坤别，固其靈根，是為靜矣。其靜也，固之專壹而不雜，此一之存也。及其春夏之時，用與坤交，播其群品，是為動矣。其動也，播之正直而不屈，此一之達也。惟一而實，故其質渾淪无外，舉地之形无不包，大可見矣。此乾以靜專動直而大生也，易之所以大者以此。夫坤純陰至順，其象為地，二而虚者也。當其利貞之際，體與乾别，斂其元化，是為靜矣。其靜也，斂之翕聚而無遺，此二之合也。及乎元亨之際，發其生意，是為動矣。其動也，發之開闢而无限，此二之分也。惟二而虚，故其量宏闊无疆，盡天之氣无不容，廣可知矣。是坤以靜翕動闢而廣生也，易之所以廣者以此。抑攷此章，上文言易廣矣大矣，此言乾大生、坤廣生，而下文遂言廣大配天地。
translation_en:
…concentrated and direct, its substance therefore embraces everything, and it generates on a great scale; since Kun gathers in and opens out, its capacity accommodates everything, and it generates on a broad scale. Is this not why the Changes is broad and great? Let us consider this: the Way of the Changes is broad indeed, and great indeed, and the source of its breadth and greatness lies in Qian and Kun.

Qian is pure yang and supremely vigorous. Its image is Heaven; it is one and solid. During autumn and winter, its substance remains distinct from Kun, and it secures its numinous root: this constitutes stillness. In stillness, it secures that root with undivided concentration and without admixture: this is the preservation of its oneness. In spring and summer, its functioning intermingles with Kun, and it disseminates the myriad kinds of beings: this constitutes movement. In movement, it disseminates them directly and without deviation: this is the expression of its oneness. Because it is one and solid, its substance is an integral whole with nothing outside it, embracing all the forms of Earth. Its greatness is thus apparent. This is how Qian, concentrated in stillness and direct in movement, generates on a great scale. Herein lies the greatness of the Changes.

Kun is pure yin and supremely compliant. Its image is Earth; it is two and empty. During the phases of benefit and constancy, its substance remains distinct from Qian, and it gathers in its primal transforming power: this constitutes stillness. In stillness, it gathers that power together, leaving nothing out: this is the union of its duality. During the phases of inception and flourishing, it releases its life-generating impulse: this constitutes movement. In movement, it releases that impulse by opening out without limit: this is the division of its duality. Because it is two and empty, its capacity is vast and boundless, accommodating all the vital energy of Heaven. Its breadth can thus be understood. This is how Kun, gathering in during stillness and opening out during movement, generates on a broad scale. Herein lies the breadth of the Changes.

Now, examining this chapter, the preceding passage says that the Changes is broad and great; this passage says that Qian generates on a great scale and Kun on a broad scale; and the following passage then says that its breadth and greatness match Heaven and Earth…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
儀則而實天之所賦若君臣嚴堂陛之威父子
正家庭之分其禮截然而不可踰也夫婦謹閨
門之别兄弟朋友篤交際之情其禮粲然而不
可紊也尊卑有等而隆殺之異宜貴賤有級而
厚薄之殊制大凡禮之所始孰非天之所定哉
然降是禮者天也而用是禮者君也夫禮難成
而易壞必為君者立之制度使禮意之嚴常藩
維于五典之間而各安其分焉禮難定而易亂
必在上者為之品則使禮文之密每流行于五
===
常之内而各盡其道焉尊卑之等着之於久而
益明貴賤之級行之於後而不僭然則人君代
天之事安民之功奚有大於是者哉嗟夫此皐
陶陳謨勉其君以安民也而必拳拳於五禮之
行者盖禮本於天而其用洋溢乎民彜物則之
間禮之不行民不可得而安矣是以其能同寅
協恭而卒成惇叙九族之治有非後世之所能
及與禮曰君臣上下父子兄弟非禮不定有虞
君臣得之矣
punctuated: 儀則，而實天之所賦。若君臣嚴堂陛之威，父子正家庭之分，其禮截然而不可踰也；夫婦謹閨門之别，兄弟朋友篤交際之情，其禮粲然而不可紊也。尊卑有等，而隆殺之異宜；貴賤有級，而厚薄之殊制。大凡禮之所始，孰非天之所定哉？然降是禮者天也，而用是禮者君也。夫禮難成而易壞，必為君者立之制度，使禮意之嚴常藩維于五典之間，而各安其分焉。禮難定而易亂，必在上者為之品則，使禮文之密每流行于五常之内，而各盡其道焉。尊卑之等着之於久而益明，貴賤之級行之於後而不僭。然則人君代天之事、安民之功，奚有大於是者哉？嗟夫！此皐陶陳謨勉其君以安民也，而必拳拳於五禮之行者，盖禮本於天，而其用洋溢乎民彜物則之間。禮之不行，民不可得而安矣。是以其能同寅協恭，而卒成惇叙九族之治，有非後世之所能及與！《禮》曰：「君臣上下父子兄弟，非禮不定。」有虞君臣得之矣。
translation_en:
…the standards governing human affairs, yet truly bestowed by Heaven. Thus ruler and minister uphold the dignity distinguishing hall from steps, and father and son maintain their respective positions within the household: their rites mark clear boundaries that cannot be crossed. Husband and wife carefully observe distinctions within the inner quarters, while brothers and friends deepen the affections of their dealings: their rites are clearly ordered and cannot be confused. Superior and inferior have their ranks, with appropriately differing degrees of ceremonial elaboration or reduction; noble and lowly have their grades, with distinct provisions for greater or lesser ceremony. In all that gives rise to ritual, what is not determined by Heaven?

Yet it is Heaven that sends down these rites, and the ruler who puts them into practice. Rites are difficult to establish but easy to destroy. The ruler must therefore establish institutions and regulations for them, so that the strictness of their underlying principles constantly safeguards the five canonical relationships, and everyone rests secure in their allotted position. Rites are difficult to settle but easy to disorder. Those above must therefore establish gradations and standards for them, so that the meticulous ordering of ritual forms continually operates within the five constant relationships, and everyone fully follows their proper way. The distinctions between superior and inferior become ever clearer as they are maintained over time; the grades of noble and lowly are observed by later generations without usurpation. What greater undertaking could there be in the ruler’s acting on Heaven’s behalf, or what greater achievement in bringing peace to the people?

Ah! In presenting his counsels, Gao Yao exhorted his ruler to bring peace to the people. His unfailing concern for the practice of the five rites arose because rites are rooted in Heaven, while their application extends throughout the enduring norms of human life and the principles governing things. If rites are not practiced, the people cannot be brought to peace. Thus ruler and ministers were able to unite in reverence and cooperate in respect, ultimately achieving a government that fostered affection and proper order among the nine degrees of kinship—an achievement beyond the reach of later ages! The Book of Rites says: “Ruler and minister, superior and subordinate, father and son, elder and younger brother: without ritual, their relationships cannot be settled.” The ruler and ministers of Youyu grasped this.

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之允迪厥德也人但見其刑制於殷民之後不
知其德著於恤功之先蓋其君也穆穆焉有和
敬之容而垂拱于九重其臣也明明焉有精白
之容而布列乎庶位明德日宣光被四表凡得
于觀感之餘者靡不滌除其舊染而從善如弗
及德輝四布丕冒海隅凡居于照臨之下者無
不興起其善心而敏德之不暇夫如是而猶有
未化之人乃不得已而有制刑之典然刑或當
輕而重則失之過或當罰而宥則失之不及故
===
必審克其中而用之於民非逞威也將匡翼之
使復其性也必折衷其是而施之於衆非任法
也將振德之使協于中也是則非德無以成恤
民之功非功無以行制刑之教此所以為刑罰
之精華而成有虞之盛治歟大抵唐虞之治用
刑非其得已也故明刑之訓常居於敷教之餘
而無刑之語即著於命刑之日穆王於訓刑之
辭能知之而不以皐陶與三后之列非輕之也
理固有所先也故曰德威惟威德明惟明刑之
punctuated: 之允迪厥德也。人但見其刑制於殷民之後，不知其德著於恤功之先。蓋其君也，穆穆焉有和敬之容，而垂拱于九重；其臣也，明明焉有精白之容，而布列乎庶位。明德日宣，光被四表，凡得于觀感之餘者，靡不滌除其舊染，而從善如弗及；德輝四布，丕冒海隅，凡居于照臨之下者，無不興起其善心，而敏德之不暇。夫如是，而猶有未化之人，乃不得已而有制刑之典。然刑或當輕而重，則失之過；或當罰而宥，則失之不及。故必審克其中而用之於民，非逞威也，將匡翼之，使復其性也；必折衷其是而施之於衆，非任法也，將振德之，使協于中也。是則非德無以成恤民之功，非功無以行制刑之教，此所以為刑罰之精華，而成有虞之盛治歟！大抵唐虞之治，用刑非其得已也。故明刑之訓，常居於敷教之餘，而無刑之語，即著於命刑之日。穆王於訓刑之辭能知之，而不以皐陶與三后之列，非輕之也，理固有所先也。故曰：「德威惟威，德明惟明。」刑之

…to make them faithfully follow their virtue. People see only that his punishments were instituted after the people had prospered; they do not realize that his virtue was manifest before his efforts to care for them. His ruler, solemn and serene, possessed a harmonious and reverent bearing and sat with folded hands deep within the palace; his ministers, discerning and enlightened, possessed a pure and spotless bearing and occupied the various offices. Their shining virtue was daily made manifest, its light reaching the four extremities. All who were influenced by observing them washed away their former corrupt habits and pursued goodness as though they could never catch up with it. The radiance of virtue spread in every direction, extending its shelter even to the remotest shores. All who lived beneath its illumination stirred their hearts toward goodness and exerted themselves in virtue as though time were insufficient. Only when, despite this, some people remained untransformed was it necessary, as a last resort, to establish a code of punishments. Yet if a punishment that should be light is made heavy, it errs through excess; if an offense that should be punished is pardoned, it errs through deficiency. Thus one must carefully ascertain the proper balance and apply it to the people—not to display power, but to correct and assist them so that they recover their original nature. One must determine what is right and apply it to the multitude—not merely to rely on the law, but to uplift them so that they accord with the mean. Without virtue, then, one cannot accomplish the work of caring for the people; without that accomplishment, one cannot carry out the instruction embodied in the institution of punishments. Is this not what constitutes the finest essence of punishment and brought about the flourishing government of Youyu?

業氣象健筆也

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
知太王之肇基耳不知至我文王小心翼翼昭
事上帝而後致多福之歸焉上帝臨女人知武
王之伐商耳不知由我文王不識不知順帝之
則而已集維新之命焉無然畔援無然歆羨明
德之懷非人力之及也曰有奔走曰有禦侮髦
士之宜是天命之臨也是以令聞之宣固崇侯
所不能譖而方國之附亦程邑所不能容于是一
征之始非佳兵也將舉義以詢仇方也三旬
之教非示弱也將施仁以附來者也赫然之怒
===
以至仁伐不仁而成無敵之勢爰整之旅以天
命討有罪而成不世之功崇墉伐而四方同立
國之規模定矣豐邑作而下民王興王之氣象
成矣是則文王之德非但以篤周祜而足以對
天下之心文王之功非但以築豐邑而欲以求
天下之定天命非文德不集武功非天命不成
此文王之所以克君也歟抑考是詩以武功稱
文王至於武王則但言其鎬京辟雝之事而已
蓋王業之成文王實造其始武王特續而終之
punctuated: 知太王之肇基耳，不知至我文王，小心翼翼，昭事上帝，而後致多福之歸焉。「上帝臨女」，人知武王之伐商耳，不知由我文王，不識不知，順帝之則，而已集維新之命焉。「無然畔援，無然歆羨」，明德之懷，非人力之及也；曰有奔走，曰有禦侮，髦士之宜，是天命之臨也。是以令聞之宣，固崇侯所不能譖，而方國之附，亦程邑所不能容。於是一征之始，非佳兵也，將舉義以詢仇方也；三旬之教，非示弱也，將施仁以附來者也。赫然之怒，以至仁伐不仁，而成無敵之勢；爰整之旅，以天命討有罪，而成不世之功。崇墉伐而四方同，立國之規模定矣；豐邑作而下民王，興王之氣象成矣。是則文王之德，非但以篤周祜，而足以對天下之心；文王之功，非但以築豐邑，而欲以求天下之定。天命非文德不集，武功非天命不成，此文王之所以克君也歟？抑考是詩，以武功稱文王，至於武王，則但言其鎬京辟雝之事而已。蓋王業之成，文王實造其始，武王特續而終之
translation_en:
…know only that King Tai laid the foundations; they do not know that only when our King Wen, ever careful and reverent, illustriously served the Lord on High did manifold blessings come to him. “The Lord on High watches over you”: people know only that King Wu attacked Shang; they do not know that through our King Wen, who without conscious knowledge or calculation followed the Lord’s pattern, the newly renewed Mandate had already been secured. “Do not thus waver or stray; do not thus covet or envy”: cherishing luminous virtue is beyond what human effort alone can attain. The poem speaks of those who hasten to serve and those who ward off aggression: that eminent men should find their fitting place signifies the arrival of Heaven’s Mandate. Thus the spreading of his excellent reputation could certainly not be checked by the slanders of the Marquis of Chong, while the regional states that rallied to him could no longer be accommodated at Cheng.

Hence, when he first undertook his campaign, it was not because he delighted in arms, but because he intended to raise a righteous force and take counsel concerning the enemy state. His instruction over thirty days was no display of weakness: he intended to extend benevolence and draw to himself those who came over. In his blazing wrath, he employed the utmost benevolence to attack the unbenevolent, thereby attaining an invincible position. With his troops duly arrayed, he invoked Heaven’s Mandate to punish the guilty, thereby accomplishing a deed rarely equaled in any age. When Chong’s walls were attacked and the four quarters united, the framework for establishing the state was settled. When the settlement at Feng was built and the common people acknowledged him as king, the signs of a rising royal order were complete.

Thus King Wen’s virtue not only increased Zhou’s blessings but also sufficed to answer the hearts of all under Heaven. King Wen’s achievement was not merely to build Feng: his purpose was to seek peace for all under Heaven. Without civil virtue, Heaven’s Mandate does not converge upon a ruler; without Heaven’s Mandate, military achievement cannot be brought to completion. Was this not why King Wen was able to rule? Yet, examining this poem, we find that it praises King Wen for military achievements, whereas for King Wu it speaks only of his capital at Hao and its royal ceremonial school. For in the completion of the royal enterprise, it was King Wen who truly laid its beginnings, while King Wu merely carried it forward and brought it to completion…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
昭于天文王之神在天者大矣今我得天下之
懽心以奉其祀亦將陟降于庭以安我思成之
孝乎於穆清廟文王之主在廟者遠矣今我得
天下之備物以行其祭亦將昭假于𫝊以慰我
孝子之心乎然先王之假不可度先王之德不
可忘蓋維宣維哲而有緝熈之敬人道盡矣允
文允武而有伊濯之功君道備矣故下安乎人
而民心歸上及乎天而天道應施于孫子以膺
大統之傳肇啓後人以綿世德之嗣何以安我
===
而以萬壽維壽可以永天命也何以助我而以
多福維福可以保天位也是以使我得率此諸
侯而尊于顯烈之文考者何莫非先德之所及
耶使我得薦此備禮而享于文德之聖母者何
莫非德澤之所庇耶吁武王于宗廟之祭所以
致孝于巳而歸德于先王者何其至哉抑觀武
王之祭文王以天子之尊致天下之享竭孝思
之誠可謂盛矣而先王之神其有不享者乎及
其歌此詩以徹也猶若不敢必者而維稱其功
punctuated:
昭于天，文王之神在天者大矣！今我得天下之懽心以奉其祀，亦將陟降于庭，以安我思成之孝乎？於穆清廟，文王之主在廟者遠矣！今我得天下之備物以行其祭，亦將昭假于𫝊，以慰我孝子之心乎？然先王之假不可度，先王之德不可忘。蓋維宣維哲，而有緝熈之敬，人道盡矣；允文允武，而有伊濯之功，君道備矣。故下安乎人而民心歸，上及乎天而天道應，施于孫子以膺大統之傳，肇啓後人以綿世德之嗣。何以安我？而以萬壽維壽，可以永天命也。何以助我？而以多福維福，可以保天位也。是以使我得率此諸侯，而尊于顯烈之文考者，何莫非先德之所及耶？使我得薦此備禮，而享于文德之聖母者，何莫非德澤之所庇耶？
吁！武王于宗廟之祭，所以致孝于巳而歸德于先王者，何其至哉！抑觀武王之祭文王，以天子之尊，致天下之享，竭孝思之誠，可謂盛矣，而先王之神其有不享者乎？及其歌此詩以徹也，猶若不敢必者，而維稱其功

…Shining in Heaven—how great is King Wen’s spirit in Heaven! Now that I have won the joyful allegiance of all under Heaven and thereby offer him worship, will he ascend and descend in the court, bringing reassurance to the filial devotion through which I seek to realize his presence? Ah, solemn is the pure ancestral temple! How remote is King Wen, whose spirit tablet stands within it! Now that I possess the full array of offerings from all under Heaven with which to perform his sacrifice, will he also gloriously draw near to [?], comforting my heart as his filial son? Yet the former king’s coming cannot be fathomed, and his virtue cannot be forgotten. Manifest in virtue and wise, he possessed an ever-brightening reverence: thus he fulfilled the human way. Truly accomplished in civil and martial affairs, he possessed magnificent achievements: thus he perfected the ruler’s way. Hence, below, he brought peace to the people, and their hearts turned to him; above, his influence reached Heaven, and Heaven’s way responded. His beneficence extended to his descendants, enabling them to receive the succession to supreme rule; he opened the way for later generations, perpetuating the inheritance of virtue through the ages. How does he bring me peace? By granting me longevity in its myriad fullness, so that I may perpetuate Heaven’s Mandate. How does he assist me? By blessing me with abundant blessings, so that I may preserve the throne conferred by Heaven. Thus, that I can lead these feudal lords in honoring my illustrious and glorious father—is any of this not the extension of his ancestral virtue? That I can present these complete ritual offerings to my sagely mother of cultured virtue—is any of this not owing to the shelter of his virtuous beneficence?
Ah! How consummate was King Wu’s performance of filial devotion on his own part [?] and his attribution of virtue to the former king in the sacrifices at the ancestral temple! Consider King Wu’s sacrifice to King Wen: with the dignity of the Son of Heaven, he presented the offerings of all under Heaven and exhausted the sincerity of his filial thoughts. This may indeed be called magnificent. Could the former king’s spirit possibly fail to accept the offerings? Yet when he sang this ode as the offerings were removed, he still seemed not to dare presume upon their acceptance, and merely extolled his achievements…

text:

宰周公序於諸侯之上者例耶故聖人變文書
及以會若曰王世子在是而諸侯咸往會焉示
不可得而抗也是非尊君之意乎逮夫襄王之

率小伯而會于葵丘適天子賜以有事文武之
===

受時宰周公寔臨會焉夫宰兼三公位尊職重

乎夫天尊地卑而其分定典叙禮秩而其義明

punctuated: 國而會于首止，仰宗廟社稷之有主，明朝覲訟獄之有歸，大本以定，王室以寧。時王世子寔出會焉。夫君臣上下，禮達分定，以王世子而下會諸侯則陵，以諸侯而上會王世子則抗，豈可與宰周公序於諸侯之上者例耶？故聖人變文，書及以會，若曰王世子在是，而諸侯咸往會焉，示不可得而抗也。是非尊君之意乎？逮夫襄王之時，內難方弭，王禁猶未明也。桓公於是合大侯，率小伯，而會于葵丘。適天子賜以有事文武之胙，後命寵以伯舅耋老之辭，加勞賜級，下拜登受。時宰周公寔臨會焉。夫宰兼三公，位尊職重，然人臣或進為三公而入乎朝廷之內，或退為方伯而出乎郊畿之外，豈可與王世子之貴有常尊者倫耶？故聖人循常書會，蓋曰三公雖貴，而亦在臣列焉，不得而殊會也。是非抑臣之義乎？夫天尊地卑而其分定，典叙禮秩而其義明，此聖人所以殊會世子以尊君，列會宰周公以抑臣也。其旨不亦深乎？抑又攷之，齊桓初會首

…states and assembled at Shouzhi, looking to ensure that the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain had their rightful lord, and making clear to whom court audiences and litigation should be directed. Thus the great foundation was secured and the royal house brought peace. At that time the king’s heir apparent indeed came out to attend the meeting. Now, between ruler and minister, superior and inferior, ritual applies throughout and distinctions of status are fixed. For the king’s heir apparent to descend to meet the feudal lords would abase him; for the feudal lords to ascend to meet the king’s heir apparent would place them on an equal footing with him. How could this be treated like the case of the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou, being listed above the feudal lords? Therefore the Sage varied his wording, using “and” to record the meeting, as if to say that the king’s heir apparent was there and the feudal lords all went to meet him, showing that they could not claim equality with him. Is this not an expression of the intent to honor the ruler?
By the time of King Xiang, internal strife had only just subsided, and the royal prohibitions had not yet been made clear. Duke Huan therefore gathered the great lords and led the lesser ones to assemble at Kuiqiu. It happened that the Son of Heaven bestowed upon him sacrificial meat from the rites for Kings Wen and Wu. A subsequent command honored him with the expressions “senior uncle” and “of advanced age,” adding commendation and a grant of rank [?]; he bowed below the steps, then ascended to receive the gift. At that time the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou, indeed attended the meeting. Now, the Grand Steward concurrently ranked among the Three Dukes: his position was exalted and his responsibilities weighty. Yet a minister might advance to become one of the Three Dukes and enter the royal court, or withdraw to become a regional overlord and serve beyond the royal domain. How could he be compared with the king’s heir apparent, whose noble standing carried an unvarying claim to honor? Therefore the Sage followed the usual practice in recording the meeting. The implication is that although the Three Dukes are exalted, they nevertheless stand among the ministers, and their attendance cannot be recorded as a distinct kind of meeting. Is this not the principle of keeping ministers in their subordinate place?
Heaven is exalted and earth lowly, and their respective stations are fixed; established norms have their order and ritual its gradations, and the proper relations are clear. This is why the Sage distinguished the meeting with the heir apparent to honor the ruler, but listed the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou, among the participants in the meeting to keep ministers in their subordinate place. translation_en:
…is greedy and wears out its people; Heaven is delivering it into our hands.” Thus the decision was made to intercept Qin’s army. These two ministers saw only the advantage of the moment, hoping for a lucky success that they could claim as an achievement. Had Duke Mu remained steadfast in supporting Jin, and had Duke Xiang remembered his debt of gratitude to Qin, rejecting the two ministers’ advice so as to perpetuate friendship between the two states, both would have been worthy rulers. Yet Qin mistakenly adopted Qizi’s plan, attacking Zheng with designs on Jin; Jin likewise wrongly heeded Xian Zhen’s strategy, taking up arms to defeat Qin. Viewed by a gentleman, Jin’s conduct was this: with the burial close at hand, its ruler forgot filial duty, hastily blackened his mourning robes and headband, and went to war. He betrayed another’s kindness and provoked its enmity, trapped its troops in a defile, and annihilated its army. These were offenses of the gravest kind; hence the Spring and Autumn Annals degraded him by referring to him merely as a “man.” Qin, for its part, lodged as a guest in another’s quarters yet plotted against its host, used another’s defection as an occasion to practice deceit, exploited another state’s vulnerability to attack it, and crossed another’s territory without mourning its bereavement. This was the way of the Di barbarians; hence the Spring and Autumn Annals degraded Qin by treating it as Di.

The two ministers saw advantage and offered their schemes; the two rulers coveted advantage and went to war against each other. This would lead rulers and ministers, fathers and sons, all to abandon benevolence and righteousness and deal with one another with profit in mind, gradually sinking to the level of barbarians and beasts, until the great human relationships were destroyed. The Spring and Autumn Annals referred to Jin’s ruler merely as a “man” and treated Qin as Di in order to uphold the human way and preserve Heaven’s principle.

Moreover, examining the outset of this campaign: Qizi certainly gave Qin his advice, but did Jian Shu not say, “The army will be worn out and its strength exhausted, while the distant host will be prepared for it”? It was because the two rulers coveted advantage and disregarded loyal counsel that not a single wheel of Qin’s chariots returned, and its regret could not undo what had happened. Jin captured three commanders, but its gain could not make good its loss. A breach arose in a single moment, and warfare continued…
