之大本也世子既有大善則天下其有不正者
哉記者論世子齒學而至此迺引古語以證之
原古語之意若曰世子者國之儲貳方主器而
執鬯將踐阼而臨朝是當有元良者也元者大
之稱良者善之謂善固不可無而亦不可以不
大是必習乎樂正所業之詩書而涵養乎大本
遵乎父師所成之德行而踐履乎大道詩以理
性情書以道政事善日以富而無一之或遺浩
浩乎不可名將如天之無不覆焉德立於其中
punctuated:
於數世。貪利之禍，一至於此，其可監哉！

禮記

一有元良，萬國以貞。

同考試官訓導朱批：「以經文講古語，殊失本旨。是篇體認親切，措辭老健，夐出衆作，必佳士也。」

考試官諭德陸批：「讀此，能令人油然生忠愛之心。」

考試官侍講學士楊批：「辭理俱優，盖深於禮者。」

惟世子有大善，則天下無不正矣。盖世子天下之大本也。世子既有大善，則天下其有不正者哉？記者論世子齒學而至此，迺引古語以證之。原古語之意，若曰：世子者，國之儲貳，方主器而執鬯，將踐阼而臨朝，是當有元良者也。元者，大之稱；良者，善之謂。善固不可無，而亦不可以不大。是必習乎樂正所業之詩書，而涵養乎大本；遵乎父師所成之德行，而踐履乎大道。詩以理性情，書以道政事，善日以富，而無一之或遺，浩浩乎不可名，將如天之無不覆焉。德立於其中
translation_en:
…for several generations. The calamity caused by greed for gain reached such a pass! Surely this offers a warning!

Book of Rites

“When the one possesses great goodness, the myriad states are thereby set right.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “To explain the ancient saying through the wording of the classic quite misses its original intent. This essay, however, grasps its meaning intimately and precisely; its phrasing is mature and vigorous, far surpassing the other compositions. Its author must be an excellent scholar.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Adviser to the Heir Apparent: “Reading this can make feelings of loyalty and loving devotion arise spontaneously in one's heart.”

Comment by Examiner Yang, Expositor-in-Waiting: “Both expression and reasoning are excellent. The author evidently has a deep understanding of ritual.”

Only when the heir apparent possesses great goodness will all under Heaven be set right. For the heir apparent is the great foundation of all under Heaven. Once he possesses great goodness, could anything under Heaven remain uncorrected? Having reached this point in discussing how the heir apparent takes his place at school according to age, the author of the Record cites an ancient saying as confirmation. Examining the original meaning of that saying, it is as if it says: the heir apparent is the state's designated successor. He now presides over the ritual vessels and holds the fragrant sacrificial wine; in time he will ascend the throne and preside over court. He must therefore possess “great goodness.” “Yuan” signifies greatness; “liang” means goodness. Goodness is indispensable, and it must also be great. He must therefore study the Poetry and Documents taught by the Director of Music, nurturing the great foundation; and follow the virtuous conduct cultivated by his paternal tutor, putting the great Way into practice. Through the Poetry he orders his nature and feelings; through the Documents he learns the way of government. His goodness grows richer each day, with no aspect omitted. Vast beyond description, it will resemble Heaven, which leaves nothing uncovered. Virtue is established within him…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
行著乎其外善日以廓而無一之不萃恢恢乎
莫能量將如地之無不載焉世子之有大善如
此則萬國豈不以之而貞乎由是甸侯綏要荒
之域國以千數而凡百辟卿士莫不脩德履行
而有正直之風所謂無反無側者是矣公侯伯
子男之封國滿萬數而凡群黎百姓莫不誦詩
讀書而有端貞之俗所謂無偏無黨者是矣古
語之旨如此記者引之所以明世子齒學則父
子君臣之道得而國治也嗟乎震主東方萬物
===
畢出見龍在田天下文明信乎一有元良而萬
國遂貞矣然世子元良非教不成古之教世子
者師保疑丞皆惟其人詩書禮樂一成其德此
所以有元良而貞萬國也故曰德成而教尊官
正而國治
賓入大門而奏肆夏示易以敬也
同考試官訓導朱 批 奏肆夏示易以敬也作者講多
輕忽此篇體貼明考據詳文足以發之經傳煥然當錄為後學式
punctuated:
行著乎其外，善日以廓而無一之不萃，恢恢乎莫能量，將如地之無不載焉。世子之有大善如此，則萬國豈不以之而貞乎？由是甸侯綏要荒之域，國以千數，而凡百辟卿士莫不脩德履行，而有正直之風，所謂無反無側者是矣。公侯伯子男之封，國滿萬數，而凡群黎百姓莫不誦詩讀書，而有端貞之俗，所謂無偏無黨者是矣。古語之旨如此，記者引之，所以明世子齒學，則父子君臣之道得而國治也。嗟乎！震主東方，萬物畢出；見龍在田，天下文明。信乎，一有元良，而萬國遂貞矣。然世子元良，非教不成。古之教世子者，師保疑丞皆惟其人，詩書禮樂一成其德，此所以有元良而貞萬國也。故曰：「德成而教尊，官正而國治。」

賓入大門而奏肆夏，示易以敬也。

同考試官訓導朱批：「奏肆夏，示易以敬也，作者講多輕忽。此篇體貼明，考據詳，文足以發之，經傳煥然，當錄為後學式。」
translation_en:
…conduct becomes manifest outwardly. His goodness grows ever more expansive, encompassing every good quality, so vast that none can measure it, like the earth, which bears all things. With such great goodness in the heir apparent, how could the myriad states fail to be set right through him? Thus, throughout the domains of the dian, hou, sui, yao, and huang zones, the states number in the thousands, and all their lords and high officers cultivate virtue and put it into practice, displaying a spirit of uprightness. This is what is meant by “neither turning back nor inclining to either side.” The enfeoffed states of dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons number fully ten thousand, and all the common people recite the Odes and read the Documents, maintaining upright and steadfast customs. This is what is meant by “without partiality or faction.” Such is the purport of the ancient saying. The compiler of the Record cites it to show that when the heir apparent takes his place in school according to age, the proper relations between father and son and between ruler and minister are realized, and the state is well governed. Ah! The trigram Zhen presides over the east, and all things emerge; “the dragon appears in the fields,” and all under Heaven shines with cultivated virtue. Truly, once there is a man of great goodness, the myriad states are thereby set right. Yet the heir apparent cannot attain such goodness without education. In antiquity, those who educated the heir apparent—the Master, Guardian, Adviser, and Assistant—were all men suited to their posts. The Odes, Documents, rites, and music together perfected his virtue. This is how a man of great goodness came into being and set the myriad states right. Hence it is said: “When virtue is perfected, teaching is honored; when officials are correct, the state is well governed.”

“When the guest enters the main gate, the music of Si Xia is played, expressing ease together with reverence.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, an Assistant Instructor: “Writers often treat lightly the explanation of ‘the music of Si Xia is played, expressing ease together with reverence.’ This essay clearly grasps the meaning and offers detailed textual substantiation. Its prose adequately brings that meaning out, illuminating the Classic and its commentaries. It should be recorded as a model for later students.”

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官諭德陸批發揮和中有敬之意最親切
考試官侍講學士楊批此作非博學善說者不能及此
當迎賓而奏宜用之樂示和中有嚴敬之節也
夫燕饗迎賓宜用肆夏之樂也迎賓而用肆夏
者亦惟示和易中有嚴敬之節耳請詳陳之凡
為君者賓至必有燕饗之禮而燕饗必有宜用
之樂若行燕禮而賓入於寢門之時凡樂若王
夏昭夏皆不奏也獨用肆夏之詩播之于鐘鼓
焉行饗禮而賓入於廟門之時凡樂若章夏齊
===
夏皆不作也惟取肆夏之章宣之于金奏焉夫
所以不奏他樂而奏肆夏者何耶惟示易以敬
耳盖樂由陽来以合情也而肆夏之詩則言天
子之震疊乎諸侯聞之者皆悚然故迎賓而奏
之所以示和悦中有莊敬之節也樂由天作以
道和也而肆夏之篇則言天子之式序乎在位
聽之者皆肅然故延賓而奏之所以示樂易中
有嚴憚之意也夫和易則賓主之情不離嚴敬
則賓主之情不流此所以得禮樂之道也若文
punctuated:
考試官諭德陸批：發揮和中有敬之意，最親切。
考試官侍講學士楊批：此作非博學善說者不能及此。
當迎賓而奏宜用之樂，示和中有嚴敬之節也。夫燕饗迎賓，宜用肆夏之樂也。迎賓而用肆夏者，亦惟示和易中有嚴敬之節耳。請詳陳之。凡為君者，賓至必有燕饗之禮，而燕饗必有宜用之樂。若行燕禮，而賓入於寢門之時，凡樂若王夏、昭夏皆不奏也，獨用肆夏之詩，播之于鐘鼓焉。行饗禮，而賓入於廟門之時，凡樂若章夏、齊夏皆不作也，惟取肆夏之章，宣之于金奏焉。夫所以不奏他樂而奏肆夏者，何耶？惟示易以敬耳。盖樂由陽来，以合情也，而肆夏之詩則言天子之震疊乎諸侯，聞之者皆悚然，故迎賓而奏之，所以示和悦中有莊敬之節也。樂由天作，以道和也，而肆夏之篇則言天子之式序乎在位，聽之者皆肅然，故延賓而奏之，所以示樂易中有嚴憚之意也。夫和易則賓主之情不離，嚴敬則賓主之情不流，此所以得禮樂之道也。若文
translation_en:
Examiner Lu, Adviser to the Heir Apparent, comments: “The exposition of reverence within harmony is especially apt.”
Examiner Yang, Expositor-in-Waiting, comments: “Only someone broadly learned and skilled in exposition could attain what this composition achieves.”
When welcoming guests, one performs the appropriate music to show that harmony contains a measure of solemn reverence. For welcoming guests at banquets and ceremonial feasts, the music of Sì Xià is appropriate. Performing Sì Xià when welcoming guests serves simply to show that harmony and ease contain a measure of solemn reverence. Let me explain this in detail. Whenever a ruler receives guests, there must be the rites of a banquet or ceremonial feast, and these occasions must have their appropriate music. When conducting a banquet, as the guests enter the gate of the residential hall, none of the other pieces, such as Wáng Xià or Zhāo Xià, is performed. Only the verses of Sì Xià are sounded on bells and drums. When conducting a ceremonial feast, as the guests enter the ancestral temple gate, none of the other pieces, such as Zhāng Xià or Qí Xià, is played. Only the stanzas of Sì Xià are rendered on the bronze instruments.
Why is Sì Xià performed instead of other music? Simply to display ease tempered by reverence. Music comes from yang and brings feelings into accord; yet the verses of Sì Xià speak of the Son of Heaven’s awe-inspiring power over the feudal lords, and all who hear them are filled with apprehension. Thus, performing it when welcoming guests shows that harmonious pleasure contains a measure of dignified reverence. Music arises from Heaven and guides people toward harmony; yet the verses of Sì Xià speak of the Son of Heaven’s ordering of those who hold office, and all who hear them become solemn. Thus, performing it when ushering guests in shows that joyful ease contains a sense of awe and restraint. Through harmony and ease, the feelings of guest and host do not become estranged; through solemn reverence, their feelings do not become unrestrained. This is how the Way of ritual and music is attained. As for the text [?]…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
周禮鍾師奏九夏肆夏其一也國語謂周頌時
邁即所謂肆夏以其有肆于時夏之語而命之
也饗元侯則奏肆夏尸出入則奏肆夏此天子
用之者大射禮公升堂即席奏肆夏燕禮賓及
庭奏肆夏此諸侯用之者其後自晉趙文子始
僭於是大夫亦用之矣嗚呼三家歌雍季氏舞
八佾孔子得無歎乎
第貳塲
論
===
帝王以人文化成天下
同考試官訓導朱批此論脫去凡格力排艶語雍容
不迫風韻藹然盖有意乎出喧啾之羣者起敬起敬
考試官諭德陸批渾厚典則若奏雅於煩哇之塲
當有識者
考試官侍講學士楊批近時作論者多為論學繩尺
等書所誤誇誕浮靡深可厭惡此篇解説人文二字深有理
而通篇爾雅故錄以示學者
punctuated:
周禮鍾師奏九夏，肆夏其一也。國語謂周頌時邁即所謂肆夏，以其有肆于時夏之語而命之也。饗元侯則奏肆夏，尸出入則奏肆夏，此天子用之者。大射禮，公升堂即席，奏肆夏；燕禮，賓及庭，奏肆夏：此諸侯用之者。其後自晉趙文子始僭，於是大夫亦用之矣。嗚呼！三家歌雍，季氏舞八佾，孔子得無歎乎？
第貳塲
論
帝王以人文化成天下
同考試官訓導朱批：此論脫去凡格，力排艶語，雍容不迫，風韻藹然，盖有意乎出喧啾之羣者。起敬，起敬！
考試官諭德陸批：渾厚典則，若奏雅於煩哇之塲，當有識者。
考試官侍講學士楊批：近時作論者，多為論學繩尺等書所誤，誇誕浮靡，深可厭惡。此篇解説人文二字，深有理，而通篇爾雅，故錄以示學者。
translation_en:
… In the Rites of Zhou, the Bell Master performs the Nine Xia pieces, of which Si Xia is one. The Discourses of the States identifies “Shi Mai” (“Seasonal Progresses”) in the Hymns of Zhou as the piece called Si Xia, named for its phrase “extending throughout this great realm” (si yu shi xia). Si Xia is performed when a foremost regional lord is entertained at a feast, and when the personator of the ancestral spirit enters or leaves: these are its uses by the Son of Heaven. In the Great Archery Ceremony, Si Xia is performed when the duke ascends the hall and takes his place; in the Banqueting Ceremony, it is performed when the guest reaches the courtyard: these are its uses by the regional lords. Subsequently, Zhao Wenzi of Jin first usurped its use, and thereafter grand officers also employed it. Alas! The three great families sang “Yong,” and the Ji family staged the dance in eight rows. How could Confucius refrain from lamenting?
Second Session
Discourse
“Emperors and Kings Transform and Perfect All under Heaven through Human Culture”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: This discourse casts off commonplace patterns and vigorously rejects ornate language. It is poised and unhurried, with an abundance of graceful charm. Its author evidently aspires to rise above the clamorous crowd. It commands respect—indeed, respect!
Comment by Examiner Lu, Admonisher: Substantial and dignified, classical and well ordered: it is like performing the Elegantiae amid a din of vulgar music. Surely there will be those who appreciate it.
Comment by Examiner Yang, Academician Expositor: Recently, writers of discourses have often been misled by books such as Standards for the Study of Discourses (Lunxue Shengchi). Their extravagance, bombast, superficiality, and florid ornament are deeply repugnant. This essay explains the two characters meaning “human culture” with considerable insight, and its language is refined and correct throughout. I have therefore included it to show students.

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖人之治天下其必有所因乎為田者因
苗之性而藝之則茂防川者因水之性而
導之則通聖人之治天下苟無所因亦何
以化成之哉然則聖人之所因者何也曰
人文也聖人因人文以治天下而化成焉
古之二帝三王皆是也吾聞諸
聖天子之訓矣大哉
王言固萬方之所傳誦者然或有疑焉蓋謂文
者質之對人有質然後有文帝王之化成
===
天下何不以質而乃以文耶夫純樸不殘
孰為犠尊質若可貴矣然虎豹之鞹猶犬
羊之鞹文其可少乎況人文之文非對乎
質之文也然則人文謂何謂父子君臣夫
婦長幼朋友之道也天降此于人心謂之
性率此而行則曰天下之達道脩此以訓
則曰五教語其有常則謂之五典語其有
等則謂之五倫語其秩然則謂之人紀語
其粲然則謂之人文易曰文明以止人文
punctuated:
聖人之治天下，其必有所因乎？為田者因苗之性而藝之則茂，防川者因水之性而導之則通。聖人之治天下，苟無所因，亦何以化成之哉？然則聖人之所因者何也？曰：人文也。聖人因人文以治天下而化成焉，古之二帝三王皆是也。吾聞諸聖天子之訓矣。大哉，王言！固萬方之所傳誦者。然或有疑焉，蓋謂文者質之對，人有質然後有文，帝王之化成天下，何不以質而乃以文耶？夫純樸不殘，孰為犠尊？質若可貴矣。然虎豹之鞹猶犬羊之鞹，文其可少乎？況人文之文，非對乎質之文也。

然則人文謂何？謂父子、君臣、夫婦、長幼、朋友之道也。天降此于人心，謂之性；率此而行，則曰天下之達道；脩此以訓，則曰五教；語其有常，則謂之五典；語其有等，則謂之五倫；語其秩然，則謂之人紀；語其粲然，則謂之人文。《易》曰：「文明以止，人文
translation_en:
When the sage governs all under Heaven, must he not have something to build upon? A farmer cultivates seedlings in accordance with their nature, and they flourish; one who controls a river guides its waters in accordance with their nature, and they flow freely. If the sage had nothing to build upon in governing all under Heaven, how could he transform the people and bring them to fulfillment? What, then, does the sage build upon? The answer is human cultural patterning (renwen). The sage builds upon this to govern all under Heaven, transforming the people and bringing them to fulfillment. The Two Emperors and Three Kings of antiquity all did so. I have heard this in the instructions of our sage Son of Heaven. Great indeed are the sovereign’s words! Certainly they are transmitted and recited throughout the realm. Yet some may have doubts, saying that refinement stands opposite substance, and that people possess substance before they acquire refinement. Why, then, do emperors and kings transform all under Heaven through refinement rather than substance? If unhewn wood were not damaged, who could make an ox-shaped sacrificial vessel? Substance would thus seem worthy of esteem. Yet the hides of tigers and leopards, stripped of their hair, are like those of dogs and sheep: can distinctive patterning be dispensed with? Moreover, the “patterning” in human cultural patterning is not refinement set in opposition to substance.

What, then, is meant by human cultural patterning? It means the Way governing relations between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend. Bestowed by Heaven upon the human heart, it is called human nature. Following it in one’s conduct is called the universally applicable Way of all under Heaven. Cultivating it to instruct others is called the Five Teachings. In terms of its constancy, it is called the Five Constant Norms; in terms of its distinctions of rank, the Five Relationships; in terms of its orderly arrangement, the framework of human relations; and in terms of its luminous manifestation, human cultural patterning. The Book of Changes says: “Civilized illumination joined with restraint: human cultural patterning …

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也用是觀之盖非對乎質之文乃包乎質
之文也是文也人人之所自有非外鑠之
者何待帝王以此而化成之哉盖人雖皆
有而為氣拘物蔽失焉者衆故有待於帝
王之道之也堯文思舜文明禹文命湯建
中文王允文武王建極皆人文之至著也
帝王豈以其人文之至而強人之必從哉
第因人所自有之文而道之耳故有道之
以親九族有道之以克諧底豫有道之以
===
雝雝在宫有徽五典有正德有脩人紀有
重五教為之庠序學校之制以訓之為之
宫室車服器皿之等以示之授之以三墳
五典八索九丘之書一之以朝覲會同喪
葬嫁娶隅坐贄見之禮申之以糾戒旌之
以表樹防之以移屏刑辟之法邪者匡之
枉者直之輔以立之翼以行之不罹咎者
受之攸好德者錫之優柔以俟其化漸漬
以養其成歌以勸之舞以樂之由是天下
punctuated: 也。」用是觀之，盖非對乎質之文，乃包乎質之文也。是文也，人人之所自有，非外鑠之者，何待帝王以此而化成之哉？盖人雖皆有，而為氣拘、物蔽，失焉者衆，故有待於帝王之道之也。堯文思，舜文明，禹文命，湯建中，文王允文，武王建極，皆人文之至著也。帝王豈以其人文之至而強人之必從哉？第因人所自有之文而道之耳。故有道之以親九族，有道之以克諧底豫，有道之以雝雝在宫，有徽五典，有正德，有脩人紀，有重五教。為之庠序學校之制以訓之，為之宫室車服器皿之等以示之，授之以《三墳》《五典》《八索》《九丘》之書，一之以朝覲、會同、喪葬、嫁娶、隅坐、贄見之禮，申之以糾戒，旌之以表樹，防之以移屏刑辟之法。邪者匡之，枉者直之，輔以立之，翼以行之。不罹咎者受之，攸好德者錫之。優柔以俟其化，漸漬以養其成，歌以勸之，舞以樂之。由是天下
translation_en:
…is human cultural refinement.” Viewed in this light, it is surely not refinement set against substance, but refinement that encompasses substance. This refinement is something everyone inherently possesses, not something imposed from outside. Why, then, must people await emperors and kings to transform and perfect them through it? Although everyone possesses it, many lose it through the constraints of their vital endowment and the obscuring influence of external things. They therefore need emperors and kings to guide them. Yao was cultivated and thoughtful; Shun was cultivated and enlightened; Yu displayed cultivated accomplishments; Tang established the mean; King Wen was truly cultivated; and King Wu established the supreme standard. These were all the most manifest expressions of human cultural refinement. Did emperors and kings use their own consummate refinement to compel others to follow? They merely guided people on the basis of the refinement those people already possessed.

Thus some guided people by bringing affection to the nine degrees of kinship; some by achieving familial harmony and bringing parents to contentment; and some by fostering harmony within the palace. Some promoted the five constant teachings, some rectified virtue, some cultivated the fundamental human relationships, and some gave weight to the five teachings. They established systems of local and other schools to instruct people, and distinctions of rank in dwellings, carriages, clothing, and utensils to show them the proper order. They taught them the books of the Three Ancient Records (San fen), Five Canons (Wu dian), Eight Inquiries (Ba suo), and Nine Regions (Jiu qiu). They brought them into accord through rites governing court audiences and assemblies, mourning and burial, marriage, seating in the corners of a room [?], and formal visits with presentation gifts. They reinforced these through correction and admonition, distinguished merit with markers and planted trees, and guarded against wrongdoing through laws of removal, exclusion, and punishment. They corrected the wayward and straightened the crooked, supporting people so that they could establish themselves and assisting them so that they could act. Those who incurred no blame were received; those who loved virtue were granted rewards. They treated people gently and patiently while awaiting their transformation, gradually steeping them in instruction to nurture their perfection. They encouraged them through song and delighted them through dance. Thus, throughout the realm…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之民莫不遵其教復其典仁敬孝慈之相
接煥乎其有章如天有日月星辰之文也
和柔愛敬之相交炳乎其有采如地有山
川草木之文也於變於唐風動於虞敏德
於夏表正於殷會極歸極于周天下化成
若此非有所因而能然哉苟不因其所自
有之文而欲文之則強者挺而不肯從猶
養虎而欲制以銜勒強之則搏噬矣弱者
從而不能久猶教猱而暫被以冠服久之
===
則決驟矣此帝王所以必因人文以化成
天下也歟後世諸君若漢明帝唐文皇宋
仁宗亦皆以人文治天下矣而皆不能化
成如帝王之世蓋帝王之治雖因乎民實
本諸身而漢唐宋諸君身不備乎人文而
其所以示天下者亦皆文之末耳其安能
以化成哉洪惟我
朝
太宗文皇帝性全人文嘗命儒臣脩五經四書
punctuated:
之民莫不遵其教，復其典。仁敬孝慈之相接，煥乎其有章，如天有日月星辰之文也；和柔愛敬之相交，炳乎其有采，如地有山川草木之文也。於變於唐，風動於虞，敏德於夏，表正於殷，會極歸極于周。天下化成若此，非有所因而能然哉？苟不因其所自有之文而欲文之，則強者挺而不肯從，猶養虎而欲制以銜勒，強之則搏噬矣；弱者從而不能久，猶教猱而暫被以冠服，久之則決驟矣。此帝王所以必因人文以化成天下也歟？
後世諸君，若漢明帝、唐文皇、宋仁宗，亦皆以人文治天下矣，而皆不能化成如帝王之世。蓋帝王之治，雖因乎民，實本諸身，而漢唐宋諸君身不備乎人文，而其所以示天下者，亦皆文之末耳，其安能以化成哉？
洪惟我朝太宗文皇帝，性全人文，嘗命儒臣脩五經四書
translation_en:
…the people all followed their teachings and returned to their established norms. In their dealings with one another through benevolence, reverence, filial devotion, and parental kindness, they displayed a splendid order, like the patterns of the sun, moon, and stars in heaven. In their exchanges through harmony, gentleness, affection, and respect, they displayed a brilliant beauty, like the patterns of mountains, rivers, plants, and trees on earth. Under Tang—that is, Yao—they were gloriously transformed; under Yu—that is, Shun—they responded as if moved by the wind; under the Xia they diligently cultivated virtue; under the Yin they were set right by the ruler’s example; and under the Zhou they gathered about and turned toward the supreme standard. Could the realm have attained such transformation without something upon which to build? If one sought to refine people without building upon the patterns they inherently possessed, the strong would resist and refuse to comply. This would be like raising a tiger and trying to control it with a bit and bridle: force it, and it will strike and bite. The weak would comply but could not persist. This would be like training a monkey and dressing it briefly in a cap and robes: in time it will break loose and dash away. Is this not why the ancient emperors and kings necessarily built upon human culture to transform and perfect the realm?
Later rulers, such as Emperor Ming of the Han, Emperor Wen of the Tang, and Emperor Renzong of the Song, likewise governed the realm through human culture. Yet none could achieve transformation and perfection comparable to the age of the ancient emperors and kings. Although the government of those ancient rulers built upon the people, it was actually rooted in their own persons. The rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song did not fully embody human culture, and what they displayed to the realm was merely its superficial manifestations. How could they thereby transform and perfect it?
We reverently reflect that Emperor Taizong Wen of our dynasty fully embodied human culture in his nature. He once ordered his Confucian officials to compile the Five Classics and Four Books…

text:

筆於獲麟尚有述者綱目訖書於顯德可
無繼之

之褒鉞

天而頒降下拜登受快瞻
雲漢之昭回口誦心惟稍窺山海之藏納大

What deserved inclusion was included, and what deserved deletion was deleted, making the historical record shine through a hundred volumes. Bowing low and ascending to receive it, we rejoiced to behold the radiant brilliance of your celestial writing. Reciting it aloud and pondering it in our hearts, we gained some glimpse of its contents, as capacious as mountains and seas. Its broad outlines and numerous particulars are all presented, in detail or in summary as appropriate; legitimate dynasties and intercalary regimes are all recorded, in matters great and small. The words, deeds, and affairs of government of twenty-five rulers, read repeatedly, come together in our minds; more than four hundred years of order and disorder, rise and fall, can be surveyed in a single morning as though displayed upon our palms. 對天之洪休揚厲無前之偉績此作得之
太極分寓而德有體用之殊氣化洊出而
世有古今之異貫體用而為一者知道之
至言也合古今而無間者盡道之至聖也
然則德功言豈可使為三而我
朝
一祖四宗與古之聖帝明王亦何以異哉昔穆
===
叔謂太上立德其次立功其次立言盖德
為體而功言皆為用固自有等差者而杜
預因謂黃帝堯舜立德禹稷立功史佚周
任臧文仲立言則各舉其著者但以史周
臧三氏次於數聖人則過矣若中極而論

punctuated:
聖德神功之盛無遺，要是知所學者矣。
考試官侍講學士楊批：鋪張對天之洪休，揚厲無前之偉績，此作得之。
太極分寓，而德有體用之殊；氣化洊出，而世有古今之異。貫體用而為一者，知道之至言也；合古今而無間者，盡道之至聖也。然則德功言豈可使為三，而我朝一祖四宗與古之聖帝明王亦何以異哉？昔穆叔謂：「太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。」盖德為體，而功言皆為用，固自有等差者。而杜預因謂黃帝、堯、舜立德，禹、稷立功，史佚、周任、臧文仲立言，則各舉其著者。但以史、周、臧三氏次於數聖人，則過矣。若中極而論，則功言皆出於德，固合為一，而數聖人之德功言又烏有一之不立者？是皆如明問所云，無他說也。自禹而降，君天下者，惟商湯懋昭大德，齊聖廣淵，而其功則伐桀救

…the fullness of sagely virtue and divine achievements, omitting nothing. In sum, this is someone who understands what he has studied.
Examiner Yang, Academician Expositor-in-waiting, comments: This composition succeeds in elaborating the magnificent blessings that answer Heaven and extolling great achievements without precedent.
The Supreme Ultimate resides separately in individual things, and virtue thus has its distinction between substance and function; the transformations of vital energy emerge successively, and the world thus has its distinction between antiquity and the present. To unite substance and function as one is the consummate teaching of those who understand the Way; to join antiquity and the present without a gap is the work of the consummate sage who fully realizes the Way. How, then, could virtue, achievement, and words be treated as three separate things? And how could our dynasty’s one ancestral emperor and four succeeding emperors differ from the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity?
Formerly, Mu Shu said: “Highest is establishing virtue; next is establishing achievements; next is establishing words.” Virtue is the substance, while achievements and words are its functions, so there are indeed distinctions of rank among them. Du Yu accordingly said that the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun established virtue; Yu and Ji established achievements; and Shi Yi, Zhou Ren, and Zang Wenzhong established words. In each case, he cited what was most conspicuous about them. But to rank Shi, Zhou, and Zang immediately after those sages was mistaken. If we discuss the matter according to the central standard [?], achievements and words both issue from virtue and are therefore united as one. Moreover, among those sages, was there any who failed to establish even one of the three—virtue, achievements, and words? All this accords with what your illuminating question states; there is no other explanation.

祖宗之功在洪武時則
肇闢乾坤再造日月興綱常倫紀於百年殄
滅之餘滌山川草木於群羶汚染之後吏
士兵民搜剔其利弊殆盡禮樂刑政振舉
punctuated:
民，表正萬邦，其言則具載于《夏書》，不待舉也。周文武緝熈敬止，世德作求，而其功則誕受多方，永清四海，其言則咸在于《周書》，無俟數也。是三聖人者，乃可與前數聖人並矣。自漢而下，雖有英君誼辟以德功言稱於當時者，然豈可與數聖人並哉？惟我朝之一祖四宗，迺能與之並矣。且以德言之，若太祖高皇帝之聖神文武、欽明啓運，太宗文皇帝之體天弘道、聖武神功，仁宗昭皇帝之純誠至德、弘文欽武，宣宗章皇帝之憲天崇道、英明神聖，英宗睿皇帝之仁明誠敬、昭文憲武，皆不可以盡言也。
若稽祖宗之功，在洪武時，則肇闢乾坤，再造日月，興綱常倫紀於百年殄滅之餘，滌山川草木於群羶汚染之後，吏士兵民搜剔其利弊殆盡，禮樂刑政振舉
translation_en:
…the people and set a correct example for the myriad states. His words are fully recorded in the Documents of Xia and need not be cited here. Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou continued to shine in virtue and remained reverent, seeking to perpetuate their forebears’ virtue. Their achievements were to receive dominion over the many regions and bring lasting peace to all within the four seas. Their words are all preserved in the Documents of Zhou and need not be enumerated. These three sages may indeed stand alongside the several sages mentioned earlier. From the Han onward, although there were outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns celebrated in their own times for virtue, achievements, and words, how could they stand alongside those sages? Only our dynasty’s one founding ancestor and four ancestral sovereigns can stand alongside them. To speak first of virtue: Taizu, the Gao Emperor, was sagely and inspired, accomplished in civil and military affairs, reverent and discerning, and inaugurated the dynastic mandate; Taizong, the Wen Emperor, embodied Heaven and enlarged the Way, possessing sagely martial prowess and wondrous achievements; Renzong, the Zhao Emperor, possessed pure sincerity and consummate virtue, promoted civil culture, and esteemed military affairs; Xuanzong, the Zhang Emperor, modeled himself on Heaven and honored the Way, and was outstanding, discerning, inspired, and sagely; Yingzong, the Rui Emperor, was humane, discerning, sincere, and reverent, and made civil culture illustrious and exemplified martial virtue. None of these virtues can be fully expressed in words.
If we examine the achievements of our imperial ancestors, during the Hongwu reign Heaven and Earth were opened anew, and the sun and moon were fashioned afresh. The cardinal bonds, constant virtues, and norms of human relationships were revived after a hundred years of destruction; mountains, rivers, plants, and trees were cleansed after their defilement by the stinking hordes. In matters concerning officials, scholars, soldiers, and commoners, benefits and abuses were sought out and sifted through almost exhaustively; rites, music, punishments, and government were restored and put into effect…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
其綱目無遺復華風於三代定
國祚於萬年矣在永樂時則
既平內難載建
皇都訖聲教於四海明理學於萬方昉置交
南之郡縣盡空漠北之穹廬矣在洪熙時
則
勵志圖治推誠任人施沛澤於臣民覃至仁
於方夏矣在宣德時則
定難靖虜減稅輕刑海宇內寧而外謐
===
邦家上恬而下熈矣在正統時則
責任公孤擇牧選將下罷貢蠲逋之詔創課
種備荒之制均徭讞獄督教重儒乃致時
和歲豐而天下獲家給人足之樂政平訟
理而萬民有遷善敏德之休矣若考
祖宗之言則有
大誥三編
為善陰隲孝順事實二典與
五倫一書性理大全書序五倫書序此皆布
punctuated:
其綱目無遺，復華風於三代，定國祚於萬年矣。在永樂時，則既平內難，載建皇都，訖聲教於四海，明理學於萬方，昉置交南之郡縣，盡空漠北之穹廬矣。在洪熙時，則勵志圖治，推誠任人，施沛澤於臣民，覃至仁於方夏矣。在宣德時，則定難靖虜，減稅輕刑，海宇內寧而外謐，邦家上恬而下熈矣。在正統時，則責任公孤，擇牧選將，下罷貢蠲逋之詔，創課種備荒之制，均徭讞獄，督教重儒，乃致時和歲豐，而天下獲家給人足之樂；政平訟理，而萬民有遷善敏德之休矣。
若考祖宗之言，則有《大誥》三編，《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》二典與《五倫》一書、《性理大全書序》、《五倫書序》，此皆布
translation_en:
…leaving none of their main principles or detailed provisions unattended, restoring the Chinese civilization of the Three Dynasties, and securing the dynasty’s tenure for ten thousand years. In the Yongle reign, having quelled internal strife, he established the imperial capital anew, extended his civilizing influence throughout the Four Seas, and illuminated the Learning of Principle in every region. He first established prefectures and counties in Jiaonan and emptied the domed tents north of the desert. In the Hongxi reign, he resolved to achieve good government and entrusted men with responsibilities in sincere confidence, bestowing abundant favor upon officials and people and extending the utmost benevolence throughout the Chinese realm. In the Xuande reign, he quelled disturbances and pacified the enemy, reduced taxes and lightened punishments. The realm enjoyed peace within and tranquility without; those above were at ease and those below flourished. In the Zhengtong reign, he charged the Three Dukes and Three Solitary Ones with responsibilities, selected local governors and military commanders, issued edicts abolishing tribute exactions and remitting arrears, and instituted measures to encourage cultivation and prepare against famine. He equalized labor services, adjudicated criminal cases, supervised education, and honored Confucian scholars. Thus the seasons were harmonious and the harvests abundant, and throughout the realm households enjoyed ample provision and individuals had enough. Government was equitable and litigation properly settled, while all the people enjoyed the blessings of advancing toward goodness and diligently cultivating virtue.
If we examine the words of the imperial ancestors, there are the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), the two canonical works Doing Good and Receiving Hidden Blessings (Weishan Yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi), the book Five Human Relationships (Wulun), the Preface to the Complete Compendium of Nature and Principle, and the Preface to the Book of the Five Human Relationships. All these were disseminated…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之天下家傳而人誦者其他若
洪範註若精誠録若望江樓之記若風伯頌
之辨若招隱之歌若幸史館之詩或勒之
金石而已傳或藏之舘閣而未布者動數
千篇至數百卷詎能悉數之哉以是觀之
則我
祖宗之德功言不特並古聖人而且有過之者
矣愚生雖長育於畿甸之中游歌於
輦轂之下而聞見淺狹不能究知其萬一然
===
天地造化之妙不可得以形容也
雲漢奎璧之光不可得而繪畫也愚生之疎
畧其亦可恕矣
第二問
同考試官學正王 批 處置四民深得時宜
既不失於迂亦不入於刻書生而能如此有用之學也
考試官諭德陸 批 四民一策條目繁多而區
畫井井有要其識可知
punctuated:
之天下，家傳而人誦者。其他若《洪範註》，若《精誠録》，若《望江樓之記》，若《風伯頌之辨》，若《招隱之歌》，若《幸史館之詩》，或勒之金石而已傳，或藏之舘閣而未布者，動數千篇，至數百卷，詎能悉數之哉？以是觀之，則我祖宗之德功言，不特並古聖人，而且有過之者矣。愚生雖長育於畿甸之中，游歌於輦轂之下，而聞見淺狹，不能究知其萬一。然天地造化之妙，不可得以形容也；雲漢奎璧之光，不可得而繪畫也。愚生之疎畧，其亦可恕矣。
第二問
同考試官學正王批：「處置四民，深得時宜。既不失於迂，亦不入於刻。書生而能如此，有用之學也。」
考試官諭德陸批：「四民一策，條目繁多，而區畫井井有要，其識可知。」
translation_en:
…throughout the realm, handed down in every household and recited by everyone. Other works include the Commentary on the Great Plan, the Record of Sincerity, the Account of Wangjiang Tower, the Disquisition on the Eulogy to the Wind Earl, the Song Summoning the Recluse, and the Poem on an Imperial Visit to the Historiography Institute. Some have been engraved on metal or stone and already circulated; others remain stored in the imperial libraries and have not yet been disseminated. They readily number thousands of pieces, amounting to hundreds of fascicles. How could one enumerate them all? Viewed in this light, the virtue, achievements, and words of our imperial ancestors not only equal those of the ancient sages but even surpass them. Although this humble student grew up in the metropolitan region and wandered and sang beneath the imperial carriage, my experience and knowledge are shallow and narrow: I cannot fully comprehend even one ten-thousandth of them. Yet the wonders of Heaven and Earth's creative transformations cannot be described, nor can the radiance of the Milky Way and the Kui and Bi constellations be captured in a painting. The omissions and inadequacies of this humble student may therefore perhaps be forgiven.
Second Question
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “His arrangements for the four groups of the people accord very well with the needs of the times. They neither lapse into impracticality nor descend into harshness. For a student to achieve this demonstrates learning of practical use.”
Examiner Lu, Admonisher, comments: “This policy essay on the four groups of the people contains numerous topics and details, yet its arrangements are orderly and grasp the essentials. From this one can discern his judgment.”

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍講學士楊批言處四民之道歸在得人
而引力行何如一語結之最當
考言者當折其衷處事者當得其要夫經
傳四民之說雜矣固儒者所當考近世四
民之病夥矣尤儒者所當處考之而折其
衷處之而得其要是非承學之所能也然
明問諄諄不容以默請試言之而執事擇
焉古有四民曰士曰農曰工曰商而已在
古之帝王未有外此而稱治者然羲農十
===
三卦尚象之制器有耒耜教耕以興農有
日中為市以通商疑不及於士工也蓋卦
畫無與士工合有故不及之抑工制諸器
固已預其中矣虞九官之命稷播穀垂共
工疑不及於士商也然契之敷教已及士
稷之懋遷已及商矣周禮太宰以八則治
都鄙其三曰廢置以馭其吏四曰禄位以
馭其士五曰賦貢以馭其民八曰田役以
馭其眾而無所謂馭農工商者非遺之也
punctuated:
考試官侍講學士楊批：言處四民之道，歸在得人，而引「力行何如」一語結之，最當。

考言者當折其衷，處事者當得其要。夫經傳四民之說雜矣，固儒者所當考；近世四民之病夥矣，尤儒者所當處。考之而折其衷，處之而得其要，是非承學之所能也。然明問諄諄，不容以默，請試言之，而執事擇焉。古有四民，曰士，曰農，曰工，曰商而已。在古之帝王，未有外此而稱治者。然羲農十三卦尚象之制器，有耒耜教耕以興農，有日中為市以通商，疑不及於士工也。蓋卦畫無與士工合，有故不及之，抑工制諸器，固已預其中矣。虞九官之命，稷播穀，垂共工，疑不及於士商也。然契之敷教已及士，稷之懋遷已及商矣。《周禮》太宰以八則治都鄙，其三曰廢置以馭其吏，四曰禄位以馭其士，五曰賦貢以馭其民，八曰田役以馭其眾，而無所謂馭農工商者，非遺之也。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Yang, Academician Expositor-in-waiting: His discussion of how to arrange the four occupations ultimately rests on obtaining the right people. Concluding with the quoted phrase “How does this compare with putting it into practice?” is most apt.

Those who examine statements should reach a balanced judgment; those who handle affairs should grasp their essentials. The accounts of the four occupations in the classics and their commentaries are diverse, and certainly require scholars’ examination. The problems afflicting the four occupations in recent times are numerous, and even more urgently require scholars’ attention. To examine these accounts and reach a balanced judgment, and to address these problems and grasp their essentials, is beyond the ability of one who merely receives instruction. Yet your discerning question is so earnest that I cannot remain silent. Allow me to offer an account for you, honored examiners, to judge.

In antiquity there were just four occupations: scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants. No emperor or king of antiquity achieved good government outside this framework. Yet in the making of implements modeled on the images of the thirteen hexagrams associated with Fuxi and Shennong, there were plows to teach cultivation and promote agriculture, and markets held at midday to facilitate commerce; it seems that scholars and artisans were not included. Perhaps the hexagram figures had no correspondence with scholars and artisans, and there was thus a reason for omitting them [?]; or perhaps artisans, as makers of the various implements, were already included.

In the appointment of the nine officials under Yu Shun, Ji sowed grain and Chui directed the artisans; it seems that scholars and merchants were not included. Yet Xie’s spreading of instruction already encompassed scholars, and Ji’s promotion of the exchange of goods already encompassed merchants.

In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand Steward governs the domains and dependencies through eight regulations. The third is dismissal and appointment, by which he controls their officials; the fourth is stipends and ranks, by which he controls their scholars; the fifth is taxes and tribute, by which he controls their people; and the eighth is agricultural labor service, by which he controls their multitudes. Although none expressly mentions controlling farmers, artisans, or merchants, this does not mean that they were overlooked. …

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
職貢所馭之民即農工商之謂矣太宰以
九職任萬民一曰三農生九穀五曰百工
飭化八材六曰商賈阜通貨賄而不列士
者盖以士尚仁義業詩書而不與他民例
任之也管子謂昔聖人處四民使士就閒
燕工就官府商就市井農就四野固不雜
矣然伊尹處畎畝之中膠鬲在魚塩之市
者盖聖賢之生不可限其地也士農之子
常為士農工商之子常為工商固不遷矣
===
然狐續慶伯皆晉大夫而其後降在皂隸
孫叔敖為楚相而其子負薪者盖膏粱之
子不能世其業也胡可緣此數人而疑三
代之政哉若後世之四民雜與遷甚矣而
復有所謂釋道游手者固宜驅以合乎四
民而勢不可驟遏惟當申嚴禁令以漸損
之耳若夫四民之病則亦有可慮者大要
在於富之教之與禁之耳盖士之困於衣
食苦於待闕農之樂歳凍餒凶年流亡工
punctuated: 職貢所馭之民，即農工商之謂矣。太宰以九職任萬民：一曰三農，生九穀；五曰百工，飭化八材；六曰商賈，阜通貨賄。而不列士者，盖以士尚仁義，業詩書，而不與他民例任之也。《管子》謂昔聖人處四民，使士就閒燕，工就官府，商就市井，農就四野，固不雜矣。然伊尹處畎畝之中，膠鬲在魚塩之市者，盖聖賢之生不可限其地也。士農之子常為士農，工商之子常為工商，固不遷矣。然狐續慶伯皆晉大夫，而其後降在皂隸；孫叔敖為楚相，而其子負薪者，盖膏粱之子不能世其業也。胡可緣此數人而疑三代之政哉？若後世之四民，雜與遷甚矣，而復有所謂釋道游手者，固宜驅以合乎四民，而勢不可驟遏，惟當申嚴禁令，以漸損之耳。若夫四民之病，則亦有可慮者，大要在於富之、教之與禁之耳。盖士之困於衣食，苦於待闕，農之樂歳凍餒，凶年流亡，工
translation_en:
The people governed through occupational services and tribute are precisely the farmers, artisans, and merchants. The Grand Steward assigns the myriad people to nine occupations: the first is the farmers of the three kinds of land, who produce the nine grains; the fifth is the various artisans, who work and transform the eight materials; the sixth is the merchants and traders, who increase and circulate goods and wealth. Scholars are not listed because they esteem benevolence and righteousness and devote themselves to the Odes and Documents; they are therefore not assigned occupations on the same basis as the other people. The Guanzi says that when the sages of old settled the four groups of people, they placed scholars in quiet retreats, artisans in government establishments, merchants in marketplaces, and farmers in the countryside. Certainly, they did not intermingle. Yet Yi Yin lived among the fields, and Jiao Ge was in a market for fish and salt: the places where sages and worthies arise cannot be restricted. The sons of scholars and farmers regularly became scholars and farmers, and the sons of artisans and merchants regularly became artisans and merchants. Certainly, they did not change occupations. Yet the Hu, Xu, Qing, and Bo lineages all held office as grandees of Jin, while their descendants sank to the status of menial servants; Sunshu Ao was chief minister of Chu, yet his son carried firewood for a living. This was because sons raised in luxury could not perpetuate their families’ occupations. How could one use these few people as grounds for questioning the government of the Three Dynasties?

In later ages, intermingling and movement among the four groups became widespread. Moreover, there appeared those called Buddhists, Daoists, and idlers. They should indeed be compelled to join the four groups, but this tendency cannot be checked abruptly. One should only reiterate and enforce prohibitions strictly, gradually reducing their numbers. As for the afflictions of the four groups, these too give cause for concern. The essentials lie in enriching them, educating them, and imposing prohibitions upon them. Scholars struggle to obtain clothing and food and suffer while awaiting vacancies in office; farmers freeze and starve even in good years and wander homeless in years of famine; artisans …

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之艱於客資商之窘於征徭若此皆在於
富之也若士之玩愒不學浮華無實農之
惰而不力富而不節此皆在於教之也至
於工之作巧技以眩俗為苦器以悞人商
之表美而售惡務奢而逞慾與凡責士之
迎送急農之賦徭侵商之權利者此惟在
於禁之而已矣然論四民之病莫甚於農
而處四民之事莫重於士誠使教之與舉
之與用之莫不各盡其道而凡登庸於
===
朝著者皆端方博大之臣布列於天下者皆
循良穎達之士則自能重本而抑末興利
而除弊尚何患乎四民之有不安者哉故
曰為政在人然此皆儒者之常談而揆之
理勢有不可易者未可以常談而忽之顧
力行何如耳愚生學不足以折言之衷才
不足以得事之要姑以是復焉
第三問
punctuated:
之艱於客資，商之窘於征徭，若此皆在於富之也。若士之玩愒不學、浮華無實，農之惰而不力、富而不節，此皆在於教之也。至於工之作巧技以眩俗、為苦器以悞人，商之表美而售惡、務奢而逞慾，與凡責士之迎送、急農之賦徭、侵商之權利者，此惟在於禁之而已矣。然論四民之病，莫甚於農；而處四民之事，莫重於士。誠使教之與舉之與用之，莫不各盡其道，而凡登庸於朝著者，皆端方博大之臣；布列於天下者，皆循良穎達之士，則自能重本而抑末，興利而除弊，尚何患乎四民之有不安者哉？故曰：「為政在人。」然此皆儒者之常談，而揆之理勢，有不可易者，未可以常談而忽之，顧力行何如耳。愚生學不足以折言之衷，才不足以得事之要，姑以是復焉。

第三問
translation_en:
…the difficulty of obtaining capital for their work [?], and merchants’ distress under levies and corvée obligations: such problems all require making them prosperous. As for scholars who idle away their time without studying and display superficial elegance without substance, and farmers who are lazy rather than diligent, or wealthy yet lacking restraint, these all require educating them. As for artisans who produce ingenious works to dazzle the public and make defective wares [?] to deceive people, merchants who offer attractive exteriors but sell inferior goods, pursue extravagance, and indulge their desires, and all those who demand that scholars perform welcoming and escort duties, press farmers for taxes and corvée service, or encroach upon merchants’ rights and profits—these require only prohibition.

Yet, in discussing the afflictions of the four occupational groups, none suffer more severely than farmers; in managing the affairs of these groups, none are more important than scholars. If their education, recommendation, and employment were each conducted fully in accordance with the proper Way, so that all those raised to office at court were upright ministers of broad learning and capacity, and those stationed throughout the realm were conscientious, benevolent, perceptive, and capable officials, they would naturally give priority to the root and restrain the branches, promote benefits, and eliminate abuses. What need would there then be to worry that any of the four occupational groups might lack security? Thus it is said: “Governing depends upon people.”

These are indeed common sayings among Confucian scholars. Yet, measured against principle and practical circumstances, they contain truths that cannot be altered. They must not be disregarded merely because they are commonplace; everything depends upon how earnestly they are put into practice. This humble student’s learning is insufficient to determine the soundest judgment among competing statements, and his ability is insufficient to grasp the essentials of affairs. For now, I offer this in reply.

Third Question

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭馮批正學一策條對明盡由此而
進無若所謂棄之如弁髦則主司之得士不爽衡度矣
同考試官學正陳批仕而不學實今士子積弊
此策固將以警之耳有人能言之如此必非肯自負者可
喜可喜
考試官諭德陸批場中方嘆少策學如此卷五
策辭氣沛然亦不易得問學一篇錄其志也
考試官侍講學士楊批此士必有志於正學者非徒博
洽而已
===
讀盤盂之銘知君子無事而不學讀切磋
之詩知君子無時而不學學所以至乎道
也故自士希賢賢希聖而勗其未能仕而
學學而仕而審其未信豈有一息之可間
哉蓋君子欲窮理盡性非學不成欲修己
安人非學不達是故孔子上聖而猶有三
滅漆書之學顏子亞聖而猶有一善服膺
之學故以賈誼之才不善學而並稱孔
墨之賢以仲舒之學不窺大道而惑於
punctuated:
同考試官教諭馮批：「正學一策，條對明盡。由此而進，無若所謂棄之如弁髦，則主司之得士不爽衡度矣。」
同考試官學正陳批：「仕而不學，實今士子積弊。此策固將以警之耳。有人能言之如此，必非肯自負者，可喜！可喜！」
考試官諭德陸批：「場中方嘆少策學，如此卷五策，辭氣沛然，亦不易得。問學一篇，錄其志也。」
考試官侍講學士楊批：「此士必有志於正學者，非徒博洽而已。」
讀盤盂之銘，知君子無事而不學；讀切磋之詩，知君子無時而不學。學所以至乎道也。故自士希賢，賢希聖，而勗其未能；仕而學，學而仕，而審其未信，豈有一息之可間哉？蓋君子欲窮理盡性，非學不成；欲修己安人，非學不達。是故孔子上聖，而猶有三滅漆書之學；顏子亞聖，而猶有一善服膺之學。故以賈誼之才，不善學，而並稱孔墨之賢；以仲舒之學，不窺大道，而惑於
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: “The policy essay on orthodox learning answers the points clearly and fully. If he advances from this foundation, without doing what is called ‘discarding it like a ceremonial cap and forelocks,’ then the presiding examiners’ selection of this scholar will have accorded with the proper standards.”
Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: “Holding office without continuing to learn is indeed a long-standing failing among today’s scholars. This policy question was intended to warn them against it. Someone who can speak about it in this way surely would not willingly betray his own commitments. Most gratifying! Most gratifying!”
Examiner Lu, Admonisher of Virtue, comments: “We were just lamenting the scarcity of learning displayed in the policy essays here at the examination. A script like this, with its five policy essays so abundant in expression and vigor, is not easily found. We select the essay on learning as a record of his aspirations.”
Examiner Yang, Academician Expositor-in-Waiting, comments: “This scholar must be committed to orthodox learning; his attainment is more than extensive knowledge alone.”
Reading the inscriptions on basins and bowls, one knows that there is no activity in which the gentleman does not learn. Reading the poem about cutting and polishing, one knows that there is no time when the gentleman does not learn. Learning is the means of attaining the Way. Thus, as the scholar aspires to become a worthy, and the worthy aspires to become a sage, each strives toward what he cannot yet accomplish. Learning while serving in office, and entering office while pursuing learning, he examines what he has not yet firmly established. How could there be even a moment’s interruption? If the gentleman wishes to fathom principle and fully realize his nature, he cannot succeed without learning; if he wishes to cultivate himself and bring peace to others, he cannot achieve this without learning. Thus Confucius, though a supreme sage, still pursued learning until the lacquered writing had worn away three times; Master Yan, though second only to the sage, still pursued learning by holding fast to every good thing he acquired. Yet Jia Yi, for all his talent, did not learn properly and spoke of Confucius and Mozi together as worthies; Zhongshu, for all his learning, failed to discern the Great Way and was led astray by…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
陰陽之術管仲之尊大王室晏嬰之處死
不亂子產之精明博洽霍光之朴厚端重
非不學也而有反坫三歸澣衣濯冠鑄鼎
刑書陰妻構禍之失所學何事乎孔光之
明習漢制張禹之經學精明許敬宗之藻
警得幸柳宗元之文學絕倫非不識字也
而於進退剛正節義忠孝之字猶不識所
識何字乎韓愈大儒也而用世之學不如
王通歐陽脩大儒也而本領之學不如韓
===
愈二程夫子倡絕學於孔孟然希聖之心
至四十尚不及顏閔之無我學何難邪紫
陽朱子集大成於群儒然力行之學至晚
歲猶歎義理之無窮學豈易邪輔漢卿閉
門自守宜其究大業於俗學之中真德秀
私淑朱子宜其明正學於黨禁偽學之後
夫君子知為學之難故不能無尚友之志
多識前言往行以畜其德尚友之學也不
至於舍大逐小則豈有玩物喪志之戒哉
punctuated: 陰陽之術。管仲之尊大王室，晏嬰之處死不亂，子產之精明博洽，霍光之朴厚端重，非不學也，而有反坫三歸、澣衣濯冠、鑄鼎刑書、陰妻構禍之失，所學何事乎？孔光之明習漢制，張禹之經學精明，許敬宗之藻警得幸，柳宗元之文學絕倫，非不識字也，而於進退、剛正、節義、忠孝之字猶不識，所識何字乎？韓愈大儒也，而用世之學不如王通；歐陽脩大儒也，而本領之學不如韓愈。二程夫子倡絕學於孔孟，然希聖之心至四十尚不及顏閔之無我，學何難邪？紫陽朱子集大成於群儒，然力行之學至晚歲猶歎義理之無窮，學豈易邪？輔漢卿閉門自守，宜其究大業於俗學之中；真德秀私淑朱子，宜其明正學於黨禁偽學之後。夫君子知為學之難，故不能無尚友之志。多識前言往行，以畜其德，尚友之學也。不至於舍大逐小，則豈有玩物喪志之戒哉？
translation_en:
…the arts of yin and yang. Guan Zhong upheld the royal house’s dignity; Yan Ying remained unperturbed when facing death; Zichan was discerning and broadly learned; Huo Guang was simple, earnest, upright, and dignified. They were not without learning, yet they committed such faults as maintaining a cup-return stand and the Three Establishments [?], wearing washed robes and rinsed caps, casting penal statutes on a bronze vessel, and concealing a wife’s plotting of calamity [?]. What, then, had they learned? Kong Guang was thoroughly versed in Han institutions; Zhang Yu understood the classics brilliantly; Xu Jingzong won favor through striking literary embellishment; Liu Zongyuan was peerless in literary learning. They were not unable to read, yet they still failed to understand the words for advancing and withdrawing from office, firmness and uprightness, integrity and righteousness, loyalty and filial devotion. What words, then, did they understand? Han Yu was a great Confucian scholar, yet his learning for service in the world fell short of Wang Tong’s. Ouyang Xiu was a great Confucian scholar, yet his learning in moral fundamentals fell short of Han Yu’s.

The two Masters Cheng revived the lost learning of Confucius and Mencius. Yet, despite their resolve to emulate the sages, even at forty they had not attained the selflessness of Yan Hui and Min Ziqian. How difficult learning is! Master Zhu of Ziyang brought the achievements of the Confucian scholars to their fullest synthesis. Yet, in his learning through vigorous practice, even in his later years he still marveled at the inexhaustibility of moral principle. How could learning be easy? Fu Hanqing shut his doors and held fast to his principles; fittingly, he pursued the great undertaking amid conventional learning. Zhen Dexiu took Master Zhu as his teacher through his surviving teachings; fittingly, he illuminated orthodox learning after the partisan prohibitions against so-called false learning.

The gentleman knows the difficulty of learning and therefore cannot lack the aspiration to befriend the worthy of antiquity. To acquaint oneself widely with the words and deeds of earlier people, thereby nourishing one’s virtue, is learning through friendship with the ancients. If one does not abandon what is great to pursue what is petty, what occasion would there be for the warning that delighting in things destroys one’s resolve?

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
學優而仕仕優而學用世之學也不至於
不學從政則豈有以政為學之嫌哉或失
則多或失則寡或失則易或失則止惟學
者能一其志而四者同歸於道焉有辭章
之學有訓詁之學有儒者之學唯古者能
一其教而三者同歸於儒焉今天下經學
明於表章之後儒者出於教養之餘宜道
德日隆風教無外矣柰何為士者多以滅
裂之學而為進取之階以躁競之心而淪
===
功利之域委其故學不啻弁髦何怪乎儒
者之學不大見於世而生民之望於君子
者不能滿其欲哉嗟夫天下之治係於道
之明不明天下之道繫於人之學不學君
子之學其大如此故自序塾之學以至際
天人之化由伊洛之派以至衍洙泗之傳
為學之志舎此無他道也願執事矜其志
而教之
第四問
punctuated:
學優而仕，仕優而學，用世之學也。不至於不學從政，則豈有以政為學之嫌哉？或失則多，或失則寡，或失則易，或失則止，惟學者能一其志，而四者同歸於道焉。有辭章之學，有訓詁之學，有儒者之學，唯古者能一其教，而三者同歸於儒焉。今天下經學明於表章之後，儒者出於教養之餘，宜道德日隆，風教無外矣。柰何為士者，多以滅裂之學而為進取之階，以躁競之心而淪功利之域，委其故學，不啻弁髦？何怪乎儒者之學不大見於世，而生民之望於君子者不能滿其欲哉！嗟夫！天下之治係於道之明不明，天下之道繫於人之學不學。君子之學，其大如此。故自序塾之學，以至際天人之化；由伊洛之派，以至衍洙泗之傳，為學之志，舎此無他道也。願執事矜其志而教之。

第四問
translation_en:
“When learning leaves you strength to spare, enter office; when office leaves you strength to spare, pursue learning.” This is learning directed toward service in the world. Provided one does not undertake government without first learning, how could one incur the reproach of treating government itself as one’s schooling? Some err by attempting too much, some by attempting too little, some by taking learning too lightly, and some by stopping short. Only when learners unify their resolve can all four be brought back to the Way. There is the study of literary composition, the study of textual glosses, and the learning of Confucian scholars. Only the ancients could unify their teaching so that all three converged upon Confucian learning. Today, throughout the realm, the study of the Classics has been clarified through their public exaltation, and Confucian scholars have emerged through education and nurture. Moral virtue should therefore grow daily more eminent, and moral instruction should reach everywhere. Why, then, do so many scholars make slipshod learning a stepping-stone to advancement, and, with minds bent on impatient competition, sink into the pursuit of achievement and profit, casting aside their former learning as though it were a discarded cap or lock of hair? What wonder that Confucian learning is little manifest in the world, and that the people’s expectations of gentlemen remain unfulfilled! Alas! Order in the realm depends on whether the Way is made clear, and the Way in the realm depends on whether people learn. Such is the vast importance of the gentleman’s learning. Thus, from study in local schools to comprehending the transformations of Heaven and humanity, and from the school of the Yi and Luo rivers to carrying forward the tradition of the Zhu and Si rivers, the resolve to learn has no other course than this. I hope that you, honored sir, will look kindly upon my resolve and instruct me.

Fourth Question

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導謝批初場得子知非下士晚閱五
策辭采奪目如獲至寶後二篇出入子史或正或奇意氣奕奕
不可奈北方學者誰能先之作解京闈度其知名也久矣
同考試官學正陳批三場文字皆有英氣而五策
炫爛讀之矍然後二篇尤見才識穎異得如此士置之榜
首可無負矣
考試官諭德陸批一表五策奇偉過人後二篇尤見
精博之學美才如此必有志乎大就者一第之先吾不為子多也
===
考試官侍講學士楊批此卷義純論贍表判皆竒
五策博偉而後二篇尤眾所難到真可謂空群之驥矣
善觀天下之治者不於其政而於其勢焉
治亂安危之幾原於政而隐然綱維四疆
宇之大者勢也觀天下之於勢辟則觀宮
室之廉隅斜正而知其梁棟栴榱之美惡
舊新豈不得其要與夫以政觀天下則庶
事紛紜莫或厎定雖求其大者世所謂四
事之施亦或有不然者何則漢武帝□□
punctuated:
同考試官訓導謝批：初場得子，知非下士。晚閱五策，辭采奪目，如獲至寶。後二篇出入子史，或正或奇，意氣奕奕不可奈。北方學者誰能先之？作解京闈，度其知名也久矣。

同考試官學正陳批：三場文字皆有英氣，而五策炫爛，讀之矍然。後二篇尤見才識穎異，得如此士置之榜首，可無負矣。

考試官諭德陸批：一表五策，奇偉過人。後二篇尤見精博之學。美才如此，必有志乎大就者。一第之先，吾不為子多也。

考試官侍講學士楊批：此卷義純論贍，表判皆竒。五策博偉，而後二篇尤眾所難到，真可謂空群之驥矣。

善觀天下之治者，不於其政而於其勢焉。治亂安危之幾，原於政，而隐然綱維四疆宇之大者，勢也。觀天下之於勢，辟則觀宮室之廉隅斜正，而知其梁棟栴榱之美惡舊新，豈不得其要與？夫以政觀天下，則庶事紛紜，莫或厎定。雖求其大者，世所謂四事之施，亦或有不然者。何則？漢武帝□□
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, an Assistant Instructor: At the first session, I encountered your work and knew that you were no ordinary scholar. Later, reading your five policy essays, I found their literary brilliance dazzling; it was like acquiring a priceless treasure. The final two essays range through the philosophical masters and histories, sometimes orthodox, sometimes ingenious, with an irrepressible vitality. What scholar of the north could surpass you? You take first place in the capital’s Provincial Examination; I imagine you have long been known.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, an Instructor: Your compositions in all three sessions possess a heroic spirit, while the five policy essays are so brilliant that reading them makes one sit up in astonishment. The final two essays especially reveal exceptional talent and discernment. Having found such a scholar and placed him first on the list, we may feel that we have fulfilled our responsibility.

Comment by Examiner Lu, an Admonisher of the Heir Apparent: Your one memorial and five policy essays are extraordinary and magnificent, surpassing others. The final two essays especially reveal precise and extensive learning. Someone with such fine talent must aspire to great achievement. I do not consider first place in a single examination a sufficient distinction for you.

Comment by Examiner Yang, an Academician Expositor-in-waiting: In this script, the exposition of the classics is sound, the discourse ample, and the memorial and legal judgment both exceptional. The five policy essays are broad and magnificent, and the final two in particular attain heights that others can scarcely reach. Truly, you may be called a thoroughbred whose excellence leaves the rest of the herd without a rival.

Those skilled at assessing the governance of the realm look to its prevailing configuration of power rather than its administrative measures. The incipient tendencies toward order or disorder, security or peril originate in administration; yet what imperceptibly holds together the vast expanse of the realm’s four borders [?] is its configuration of power. Examining the realm through this configuration is like observing whether the corners of a palace are slanted or upright and thereby discerning whether its beams, ridgepoles, and rafters [?] are sound or defective, old or new. Does this not grasp the essential point? If one assesses the realm through its administrative measures, its many affairs are so tangled that no settled judgment can be reached. Even if one seeks out the major measures, the implementation of what people call the four undertakings may sometimes fail to produce the expected result. Why is this? Emperor Wu of the Han [two illegible characters]…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
吏而崇儒道捐封爵以厲儒生故公孫弘
以布衣明經超取相位降及後世士大夫
見利而趨心術蠱壞安於富貴之餘養成
柔懦之氣雖師丹何武之徒號稱持正然
不過脂韋於庶事之間而不知致主求賢
之務卒之前弊革而後弊生董賢去而王
氏起時則國勢陵夷於諂諛之俗矣光武
敦尚遺逸嚴察吏治延致數傳士重名節
而惡奸貪楊秉范滂之徒相繼而出屏棄
===
贓汚前後數百餘人天下肅然柰何官位
錯亂政化日湮朝野倉庫一空災異寇盜
迭見彼諸賢者不知處變有道而勞心於
按劾之間無益於朝綱之大時則國勢奄
奄於刑政之紊矣唐太宗貞觀末年斗米
三錢外戶不閉幾致刑措號稱太平然而
驕奢之習漸萌不急之營日廣徭役繁重
器服華靡閭閻之下怨謗荐興反不及貞
觀之初關中大饑率土荒儉百姓雖東西
punctuated: 吏而崇儒道，捐封爵以厲儒生，故公孫弘以布衣明經超取相位。降及後世，士大夫見利而趨，心術蠱壞，安於富貴之餘，養成柔懦之氣。雖師丹、何武之徒號稱持正，然不過脂韋於庶事之間，而不知致主求賢之務。卒之前弊革而後弊生，董賢去而王氏起，時則國勢陵夷於諂諛之俗矣。光武敦尚遺逸，嚴察吏治，延致數傳，士重名節而惡奸貪，楊秉、范滂之徒相繼而出，屏棄贓汚，前後數百餘人，天下肅然。柰何官位錯亂，政化日湮，朝野倉庫一空，災異寇盜迭見。彼諸賢者不知處變有道，而勞心於按劾之間，無益於朝綱之大，時則國勢奄奄於刑政之紊矣。唐太宗貞觀末年，斗米三錢，外戶不閉，幾致刑措，號稱太平。然而驕奢之習漸萌，不急之營日廣，徭役繁重，器服華靡，閭閻之下怨謗荐興，反不及貞觀之初，關中大饑，率土荒儉，百姓雖東西
translation_en:
…officials, while honoring the Confucian Way and bestowing enfeoffments and noble titles to encourage Confucian scholars. Thus Gongsun Hong, a commoner versed in the Classics, rose exceptionally to the position of Chief Minister. In later generations, scholar-officials rushed wherever they saw advantage. Their minds and intentions became corrupt; accustomed to wealth and rank, they cultivated a weak and timid disposition. Although men such as Shi Dan and He Wu were reputed to uphold what was right, they merely bent and accommodated themselves in the conduct of affairs, knowing nothing of the duty to bring their ruler to exemplary governance and seek worthy men. In the end, earlier abuses were eliminated only for new ones to arise: Dong Xian was removed, but the Wang clan rose. At that time, the underlying strength of the state declined amid a culture of flattery.

Emperor Guangwu earnestly honored worthy men living in obscurity and rigorously scrutinized the administration of officials. This influence extended through several reigns: scholars valued reputation and integrity and detested wickedness and greed. Men such as Yang Bing and Fan Pang emerged in succession, dismissing corrupt officials—several hundred in all—and inspiring solemn respect throughout the realm. Yet official appointments fell into disorder, good government and moral transformation faded daily, stores and granaries at court and throughout the country were emptied, and calamities, anomalies, bandits, and robbers appeared one after another. Those worthy men did not understand the proper way to respond to changing circumstances. Instead, they exhausted themselves in investigations and impeachments, doing nothing to strengthen the overarching framework of government. At that time, the underlying strength of the state languished amid disorder in penal administration.

In the final years of Emperor Taizong of Tang’s Zhenguan reign, a dou of rice cost three cash, outer doors were left unbolted, and punishments had almost fallen into disuse: the age was celebrated as one of great peace. Nevertheless, habits of arrogance and extravagance gradually emerged. Unnecessary construction projects multiplied daily, labor-service demands became onerous, utensils and clothing grew ornate and sumptuous, and resentment and criticism repeatedly arose among ordinary households. Conditions were, indeed, worse than at the beginning of Zhenguan, when Guanzhong suffered a great famine and scarcity prevailed throughout the land. Although the common people went east and west…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
就食未嘗嘆咨知上有憂憐之心而時下
勤撫之政也時則國勢病於驕侈之漸矣
宋神宗熙寧之閒勵精求治任用安石更
定法令剏立保甲增修戍壘闢地熈河然
不免爲殘民之俑召釁之端反不及祖宗
之世武畧雖微仁澤深厚財以不積爲富
兵以不用爲功也時則國勢弊於紛更之
患矣故曰善觀天下者亦於其勢而已勢
之不競其何能為抑嘗思之士風可振也
===
而仕宦之捷径不可塞惟仲舒進則公孫
弘退矣吏治可戢也而小弦之絶不可調
惟駟恊去則劉方進矣財者民之命民者
財之府理財者當先民後國治國者當為
民守財故魏徵懲逸欲之言可戒而段綸淫
巧之技可黜也邊防之險不在地利而在
人心朝廷之憂不在四夷而在百姓故富
弼布德之語可從而种諤横山之謀不可
用也然此皆政也修其政而奮起其勢誠
punctuated: 就食，未嘗嘆咨，知上有憂憐之心，而時下勤撫之政也。時則國勢病於驕侈之漸矣。宋神宗熙寧之閒，勵精求治，任用安石，更定法令，剏立保甲，增修戍壘，闢地熈河，然不免爲殘民之俑、召釁之端，反不及祖宗之世，武畧雖微，仁澤深厚，財以不積爲富，兵以不用爲功也。時則國勢弊於紛更之患矣。故曰：「善觀天下者，亦於其勢而已。」勢之不競，其何能為？抑嘗思之，士風可振也，而仕宦之捷径不可塞？惟仲舒進，則公孫弘退矣。吏治可戢也，而小弦之絶不可調？惟駟恊去，則劉方進矣。財者，民之命；民者，財之府。理財者當先民後國，治國者當為民守財。故魏徵懲逸欲之言可戒，而段綸淫巧之技可黜也。邊防之險不在地利，而在人心；朝廷之憂不在四夷，而在百姓。故富弼布德之語可從，而种諤横山之謀不可用也。然此皆政也，修其政而奮起其勢，誠
translation_en:
…seeking food, they never sighed or complained, knowing that their ruler felt concern and compassion for them and repeatedly issued measures to care for them diligently. By the later period, however, the strength of the state was ailing from the gradual growth of arrogance and extravagance.

During the Xining reign of Emperor Shenzong of the Song, he devoted himself earnestly to good government, employed Wang Anshi, revised laws and ordinances, established the baojia system of household organization, expanded and repaired frontier fortifications, and opened up territory in Xihe. Yet these measures became precedents for oppressing the people and sources of conflict. His rule thus fell short of that of his ancestors: although their military achievements were modest, their benevolence was profound and far-reaching. In fiscal affairs they counted the absence of hoarding as wealth; in military affairs they counted not employing their troops as achievement. Under Shenzong, the strength of the state was impaired by the troubles arising from incessant changes. Thus it is said: “Those skilled at assessing the realm look simply to its overall strength.” If that strength is feeble, what can be accomplished?

Yet I have reflected on this: if the ethos of scholars can be reinvigorated, can the shortcuts to official advancement not be blocked? Once Dong Zhongshu is advanced, Gongsun Hong will retreat. If official administration can be brought under restraint, can the broken minor strings not be put in tune [?]? Once Si Xie [?] is removed, Liu Fang [?] will advance. Wealth is the livelihood of the people; the people are the repository of wealth. Those who manage wealth should put the people before the state; those who govern the state should safeguard wealth for the people. Thus Wei Zheng’s words about restraining indulgence and desire should serve as an admonition, while Duan Lun’s excessively elaborate craftsmanship should be rejected. The security of frontier defenses rests not on advantageous terrain but on the people’s allegiance; the court’s source of anxiety lies not among the peoples of the four quarters but among its own common people. Thus Fu Bi’s counsel to extend benevolence should be followed, whereas Zhong E’s plan concerning Hengshan should not be adopted. Yet these are all matters of governance. To put governance in order and revive the strength of the state, indeed…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
無外於擇人而用之也故曰賢才者國之
重器得士則重失士則輕得士則政可修
而勢可復也然彼漢唐宋之政或得或失
其勢或治或亂靡然陋規未暇深論蓋嘗
即是而觀唐虞之世矣堯之治不先洪水
而先於明俊德舜之治不先蠻夷而先於
任元德俊德明於上元德任於下此所以
唐虞之治為萬世治天下之龜鑑歟末學
疎愚何足與此惟執事有明鑒焉
===
第五問
有多能之聖而後識楛矢之製有文學之
賢而後辨渡豕之書博學之有資於世尚
矣蓋微而昆蟲著而穹壤之大近而目睫
遠而標鹿之先孰非吾所當知則孰非吾
所當學乎奈何陳編溢緹匱之藏眾臆異
朱鉛之勘不能鉤玄索奧何敢貫殊析同
蓋聞青雲扶日而蟲書造於倉帝至黃帝
承之而書契大興矣莫列在庭而大韶沿
punctuated:
無外於擇人而用之也。故曰：「賢才者，國之重器。」得士則重，失士則輕。得士則政可修，而勢可復也。然彼漢唐宋之政，或得或失；其勢，或治或亂。靡然陋規，未暇深論。蓋嘗即是而觀唐虞之世矣。堯之治，不先洪水，而先於明俊德；舜之治，不先蠻夷，而先於任元德。俊德明於上，元德任於下，此所以唐虞之治為萬世治天下之龜鑑歟！末學疎愚，何足與此？惟執事有明鑒焉。

第五問

有多能之聖，而後識楛矢之製；有文學之賢，而後辨渡豕之書。博學之有資於世，尚矣！蓋微而昆蟲，著而穹壤之大，近而目睫，遠而標鹿之先，孰非吾所當知？則孰非吾所當學乎？奈何陳編溢緹匱之藏，眾臆異朱鉛之勘，不能鉤玄索奧，何敢貫殊析同？蓋聞青雲扶日，而蟲書造於倉帝；至黃帝承之，而書契大興矣。莫列在庭，而大韶沿
translation_en:
…lies entirely in selecting worthy men and employing them. Thus it is said: “Worthy talent is the state’s most precious resource.” With worthy men, the state carries weight; without them, it becomes insignificant. When worthy men are obtained, government can be reformed and the state’s strength restored. Yet the governments of the Han, Tang, and Song sometimes succeeded and sometimes failed; their circumstances alternated between order and disorder. Their inferior practices, followed without resistance, cannot be discussed at length here. Reflecting on this, I have considered the age of Tang and Yu. In governing, Yao gave priority not to the flood but to making eminent virtue manifest; Shun gave priority not to the outlying peoples but to employing men of great virtue. Eminent virtue shone above, and men of great virtue were employed below. Is this not why the government of Tang and Yu became a model for governing the realm for all ages? An ignorant and unlearned student such as myself—how could I be qualified to discuss this? I leave it to your discerning judgment.

Fifth Policy Question

Only with a sage of many abilities was the manufacture of arrows made from the ku shrub recognized; only with a worthy man versed in textual learning was the passage about pigs crossing a river correctly deciphered. Broad learning has benefited the world since ancient times! From tiny insects to the vast expanse of heaven and earth, from what is as near as our eyelashes to the remote beginnings of “biao lu” [?], what is there that we ought not to know? And therefore, what is there that we ought not to study? Yet old writings overflow the silk-covered book chests, and numerous conjectures yield conflicting textual assessments in vermilion and lead. If we cannot probe the abstruse and seek out the profound, how dare we connect what differs and distinguish what appears the same?

We have heard that blue clouds supported the sun, and that insect script originated with Cangdi, the Cang Emperor. When Huangdi, the Yellow Emperor, inherited it, writing flourished greatly. “Mo” stood arrayed in the court [?], and the Great Shao music traced its origins to…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
於帝嚳至虞舜修之而情文大備矣成湯
升陼伐桀說者謂自亳都迂道而往為仁
者之師是豈孔安國輕襲之說哉伊尹三
聘就湯說者謂以鼎俎滋味為說固進言
之義是豈莊子庖人之謂哉太公聞西伯
之養老孟子謂興自海濱遷史以為車載
於渭陽者世或聞其以釣道為說而因之
耳微子憫宗室之墊亡而自言出遜荒野
宋世家以為抱器伏軍門者彼不知武庚
===
既叛而得之耳共和之號史以為周召二
公共和王政之義魯連子歐陽修諸人則
以為時有共伯和者攝政之人而古亦無
共和書年之法是也屈平樹蘭之辭或以
為大夫樹公子蘭悞君之名朱文公則以
為託香草為君子之喻是也曾子易簀而
終說者謂檀弓出子游門人之手豈不以
其受之不當而微貶與宰我從叛而及說
者以為史遷多附會之辭豈不因衞有子
punctuated: 於帝嚳，至虞舜修之，而情文大備矣。成湯升陼伐桀，說者謂自亳都迂道而往，為仁者之師，是豈孔安國輕襲之說哉？伊尹三聘就湯，說者謂以鼎俎滋味為說，固進言之義，是豈莊子庖人之謂哉？太公聞西伯之養老，孟子謂興自海濱，遷史以為車載於渭陽者，世或聞其以釣道為說而因之耳。微子憫宗室之墊亡，而自言出遜荒野，《宋世家》以為抱器伏軍門者，彼不知武庚既叛而得之耳。共和之號，史以為周召二公共和王政之義，魯連子、歐陽修諸人則以為時有共伯和者，攝政之人，而古亦無共和書年之法，是也。屈平樹蘭之辭，或以為大夫樹公子蘭悞君之名，朱文公則以為託香草為君子之喻，是也。曾子易簀而終，說者謂《檀弓》出子游門人之手，豈不以其受之不當而微貶與？宰我從叛而及，說者以為史遷多附會之辭，豈不因衞有子
translation_en:
…under Emperor Ku; when Shun of Yu perfected it, its inner feeling and outward forms became fully developed. Cheng Tang ascended Zhu to attack Jie. Commentators say that he took a circuitous route from his capital at Bo, conducting the campaign as a benevolent ruler’s army should. Could this be an account that Kong Anguo merely adopted without due consideration? Yi Yin went to Tang after being invited three times. Commentators say that his discussion of the flavors prepared in cauldrons and served on sacrificial stands was properly a means of offering counsel. Could this mean that he was a cook, as Zhuangzi says? When the Grand Duke heard that the Lord of the West cared for the aged, Mencius says that he rose and came from the seacoast. Sima Qian’s history, however, says that he was taken up into a carriage north of the Wei River. People perhaps heard that he explained the Way through fishing and merely elaborated upon this.

Weizi grieved over the ruin of the royal house and himself spoke of withdrawing into the wilderness. The Hereditary House of Song says that he carried ritual vessels and prostrated himself at the army’s gate; its author simply did not know that this took place after Wu Geng had rebelled [?]. As for the designation Gonghe, the history interprets it to mean that the two dukes, of Zhou and Shao, jointly harmonized the royal administration. Lu Lianzi, Ouyang Xiu, and others, however, hold that there was then a man named He, Earl of Gong, who acted as regent, and that antiquity had no practice of recording years under the designation Gonghe. This is correct.

As for Qu Ping’s words about planting orchids, some take them to mean that, as a grand master, he advanced Prince Lan, who became notorious for misleading his ruler [?]. Master Zhu, posthumously titled Wen, instead takes the fragrant plants as a metaphor for gentlemen. This is correct. Zengzi had his sleeping mat changed before he died. Commentators say that the Tan Gong chapter came from the hands of Ziyou’s disciples. Might they not have subtly censured him because his acceptance of that mat had been improper? Zai Wo was implicated through joining a rebellion. Commentators hold that Sima Qian’s history contains many strained connections. Might this error not have arisen because in Wei there was someone named Zi…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
我之名而遂悮與遷史以翼儲而歸四皓
之功通鑑以其有子脅父之嫌也而削之
通鑑以辭章而畧屈平之節綱目以其有
以身事君之忠也而取之火禁當仲春之
時戒火盛也周人有其令矣而世以原介
子之燔者妄也海潮隨朔望之候乘陰盛
也儒先有是論矣而世以為憑子胥之怒
者非也庸儒鄙生相汲為誕傳襲之悮可
勝言哉嗟夫藝海源深莫窮其際風簷晷
===
短姑引其凡况無劉敞之博而妄陳入閣
之儀有韓昶之愚而繆正金根之悮惟執
事擅典章之總會號冊牘之淵林愚也願
如李北海從先達借觀秘書之心久矣幸
許其躡清塵而進焉幸甚
punctuated: 我之名而遂悮與？遷史以翼儲而歸四皓之功，通鑑以其有子脅父之嫌也而削之。通鑑以辭章而畧屈平之節，綱目以其有以身事君之忠也而取之。火禁當仲春之時，戒火盛也，周人有其令矣，而世以原介子之燔者，妄也。海潮隨朔望之候，乘陰盛也，儒先有是論矣，而世以為憑子胥之怒者，非也。庸儒鄙生相汲為誕，傳襲之悮，可勝言哉！嗟夫！藝海源深，莫窮其際；風簷晷短，姑引其凡。况無劉敞之博而妄陳入閣之儀，有韓昶之愚而繆正金根之悮。惟執事擅典章之總會，號冊牘之淵林。愚也願如李北海從先達借觀秘書之心久矣，幸許其躡清塵而進焉，幸甚！
translation_en:
…the name Ziwo, and thus fall into error? Sima Qian’s history credits the Four Hoary Elders with safeguarding the heir apparent; the Comprehensive Mirror omitted this because it suggested a son coercing his father. The Comprehensive Mirror treated Qu Ping in terms of literary composition and passed over his moral integrity; the Outline and Details included him for his loyalty in serving his ruler with his very life. The prohibition on fire fell in the second month of spring as a precaution against fire’s growing strength; the people of Zhou already had such an ordinance. The common claim that it originated in Jiezi’s death by burning is groundless. The sea’s tides follow the new and full moons, responding to the strength of yin; earlier Confucian scholars already advanced this explanation. The common claim that they are driven by Zixu’s anger is mistaken. Mediocre scholars and ill-informed students draw one another into fabrications [?]. Could the errors handed down and perpetuated ever be fully recounted?

Alas! The ocean of learning has deep sources, and its bounds cannot be exhausted. Time beneath the examination hall’s windswept eaves is short, so I have merely outlined the main points. Moreover, lacking Liu Chang’s breadth of learning, I presumptuously expound the ceremonies for entering the palace pavilion; possessing Han Chang’s foolishness, I mistakenly undertake to correct the supposed error in “golden-root carriage.” You, honored sir, command the collected institutions and precedents and are renowned as a vast repository of books and documents. I, in my ignorance, have long wished to follow Li Beihai’s example in borrowing rare writings from senior scholars to read. If you would graciously permit me to follow in your distinguished footsteps and advance, I would count myself most fortunate!

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄後序
今順天為古燕趙之地風氣
閟不洩歷數千百載以完畀
我
高皇帝既而
文皇帝顧瞻形勢北徙都之山川
草木軌文玉帛之麗煥然天
===
府之國也然其地曩稱多賢
豪人而司馬子長獲從燕趙
士游故其文豪宕有竒氣則
其人不啻沉鷙茂材力而有
文事焉乆矣乃今乘大氣而
出距往牒所登載不倍蓰以
無讓亦何所幸會於其時哉
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄後序

今順天為古燕趙之地，風氣閟不洩，歷數千百載，以完畀我高皇帝。既而，文皇帝顧瞻形勢，北徙都之。山川草木、軌文玉帛之麗，煥然天府之國也。然其地曩稱多賢豪人，而司馬子長獲從燕趙士游，故其文豪宕有竒氣，則其人不啻沉鷙茂材力，而有文事焉乆矣。乃今乘大氣而出，距往牒所登載，不倍蓰以無讓，亦何所幸會於其時哉！
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Provincial Examination

Present-day Shuntian occupies the ancient lands of Yan and Zhao. Its vital influences remained stored up, unreleased, for thousands of years, to be bestowed intact upon our Emperor Gao. Subsequently, Emperor Wen surveyed its strategic configuration and moved the capital north to this place. With the beauty of its mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees, its unified standards for carriage tracks and writing, and its ceremonial jades and silks, it shone forth as a land richly endowed by Heaven.

Yet this region had long been celebrated for its many worthy and outstanding men. Sima Zichang had the opportunity to associate with scholars of Yan and Zhao, and consequently his writing was bold and unrestrained, possessed of an extraordinary spirit. Thus its people have long excelled not only in resolute fierceness, abundant talent, and strength, but also in literary pursuits. Now they emerge borne upon this mighty vital force. Compared with those recorded in earlier histories, even if they are not twice or five times as numerous, they yield nothing to them [?]. How fortunate, indeed, to encounter such an age!

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
成化庚子屆鄉試之期臣守
陳臣簡實奉
詔來主試事稽試士之眾三千
六百有竒三十取一額鐫一
百三十五人而止因悉覩
京師游學之廣文敎之宣鬯
至矣簡聞八音與政通而文
===
章與時高下驗之來今豈當
魯兩生所謂禮樂百年而興
之期乎蓋禮樂為致治之本
而刑政以輔之此聖王之極
功皆儒者之文事也後世儒
學不明論治者方以刀筆筐
篋為能而若無預乎文言道
punctuated:
成化庚子，屆鄉試之期，臣守陳、臣簡實奉詔來主試事。稽試士之眾，三千六百有竒，三十取一，額鐫一百三十五人而止。因悉覩京師游學之廣，文敎之宣鬯至矣。
簡聞八音與政通，而文章與時高下。驗之來今，豈當魯兩生所謂禮樂百年而興之期乎？蓋禮樂為致治之本，而刑政以輔之，此聖王之極功，皆儒者之文事也。後世儒學不明，論治者方以刀筆筐篋為能，而若無預乎文，言道
translation_en:
In the gengzi year of the Chenghua reign [1480], when the Provincial Examination fell due, your servants Shouchen 守陳 and Jian 簡 received an imperial edict and came to preside over it. The candidates numbered more than 3,600; one in thirty was selected, with the prescribed quota limited to 135 men. We thus fully witnessed how extensively students flocked to the capital for study, and how thoroughly literary and moral instruction had spread.
I, Jian, have heard that the eight classes of musical sound are connected with government, and that literary composition rises and falls with the times. Judging by the present and what is to come [?], might this be the moment of which the two scholars of Lu spoke, when rites and music flourish after a hundred years? Rites and music are the foundation for achieving good government, while punishments and administration support them. These constitute the highest achievement of sage kings and all belong to the cultural work of Confucian scholars. In later ages, Confucian learning became obscure. Those who discussed government took skill with clerical documents and their storage boxes as the measure of ability, as though they had no part in cultural learning, while those who spoke of the Way…

title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
者以咕畢呻吟為功而每不
涉乎事雖以名儒若歐陽子
者猶曰文章足以潤身政事
足以及物不知文章不達於
政則晉唐之諸子有華無實
耳政事不澤於文則東漢之
三公有事無政耳何怪乎禮
===
樂不興風俗不美天下不蒙
至治之澤與方今
聖天子撫盈成之運建中和之極
而欲垂萬世之統文明之象
真百年之會也禮樂脩明刑
政齊一舉天下於風聲道化
之中以無外當其時矣而凡
punctuated:
者以咕畢呻吟為功，而每不涉乎事。雖以名儒若歐陽子者，猶曰：「文章足以潤身，政事足以及物。」不知文章不達於政，則晉唐之諸子有華無實耳；政事不澤於文，則東漢之三公有事無政耳。何怪乎禮樂不興，風俗不美，天下不蒙至治之澤與？
方今聖天子撫盈成之運，建中和之極，而欲垂萬世之統，文明之象，真百年之會也。禮樂脩明，刑政齊一，舉天下於風聲道化之中以無外，當其時矣。而凡
translation_en:
…those who regard muttering and groaning [?] as an accomplishment, yet seldom engage with practical affairs. Even a renowned Confucian scholar such as Master Ouyang said: “Literary writing suffices to adorn oneself; governmental affairs suffice to benefit others.” He did not understand that if literary writing has no application to government, the various masters of the Jin and Tang possess mere flowers without fruit; and if governmental affairs are not enriched by literary culture, the Three Dukes of the Eastern Han merely transact affairs without achieving good government. Why, then, be surprised that rites and music do not flourish, customs are not good, and the realm receives none of the blessings of perfect governance?
Now the sagely Son of Heaven presides over an age of plenitude and accomplished order, establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony, and wishes to bequeath a succession enduring for ten thousand generations. This manifestation of cultural brilliance is truly the conjunction of a hundred years. title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
藻飾之具謨明之任發揚蹈
厲之功要非俗吏所能而必
委之禮文儒術之士也諸賢
資於文以自獻矣尚無文勝
而質敝名成而行隳日紛輪
於功利之場以壞其故業異
時舉而措之豈無可仰副
===
聖明敷求之典更化之心而裨萬
分之一者乎若量其才可為
外內大小百執事之流儷時
所稱其人者是必在所優焉
而不以是靳之也且筮進之
志猶初達之泉導之為溝澮
則溝澮為川則川海則海百
punctuated: 藻飾之具、謨明之任、發揚蹈厲之功，要非俗吏所能，而必委之禮文儒術之士也。諸賢資於文以自獻矣，尚無文勝而質敝、名成而行隳，日紛輪於功利之場，以壞其故業。異時舉而措之，豈無可仰副聖明敷求之典、更化之心，而裨萬分之一者乎？若量其才，可為外內大小百執事之流，儷時所稱其人者，是必在所優焉，而不以是靳之也。且筮進之志，猶初達之泉，導之為溝澮則溝澮，為川則川，海則海。百
translation_en:
…the means of cultural embellishment, the responsibility for enlightened deliberation, and the work of vigorous, spirited expression are certainly beyond the abilities of ordinary functionaries: they must be entrusted to men versed in ritual culture and Confucian learning. You gentlemen have drawn upon your literary accomplishments to present yourselves for service. May you avoid letting refinement prevail while substance decays, or reputation flourish while conduct deteriorates, daily embroiling yourselves [?] in the pursuit of profit and advancement and thereby ruining your previous attainments. When, in time, you put your learning into practice, surely there will be something through which you can fulfill the sagely ruler’s purpose in seeking worthy men far and wide and his desire to transform governance, contributing even one ten-thousandth to that endeavor?

If, in assessing your talents, one finds you fit to join the many officials serving outside or within the capital, in greater or lesser offices, and to match those whom the age praises as suited to their posts, this surely lies well within your abilities; I would not begrudge you that recognition. title: 成化十六年順天府鄉試錄
text:
川之東固思所以為諸賢導
耳錄成簡當題于後宣
聖化以風厲乎天下盖畿內事也
非若侯邦要服之限於其務
者也敢論其大如此
奉訓大夫右春坊右諭德陸
簡謹序
punctuated:
川之東，固思所以為諸賢導耳。錄成，簡當題于後，宣聖化以風厲乎天下，盖畿內事也，非若侯邦要服之限於其務者也。敢論其大如此。
奉訓大夫、右春坊右諭德陸簡謹序。
translation_en:
…as the rivers flow eastward, I have indeed been considering only how to guide these worthy men. Now that the record is complete, I, Jian, am to append some words at its end. To proclaim the sage emperor’s transforming influence and thereby inspire and encourage all under Heaven is, after all, the responsibility of the metropolitan region. It is unlike the feudal domains and the distant zones of submission, whose responsibilities are confined to their own affairs. Thus I venture to discuss the larger significance of this undertaking.
Respectfully prefaced by Lu Jian, Grand Master for Rendering Instruction and Right Mentor of the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.
